item.title: Finance Pulse - Nov 26, 2026
item.description:
I now have strong, fresh, sourced material for today's Thanksgiving Day episode. The genuinely new developments are: (1) October PCE landed today, Thanksgiving, with headline at three point eight percent and core at three point three percent, beating the three point two percent forecast -- the highest core reading in nearly three years; (2) Kalshi markets have firmed the December hike back to ninety-three percent probability after the Bessent-driven uncertainty from the Nov 24 episode; (3) the Q2/November deposit pricing data showing fixed-rate cost-of-funds rising sharply with the twelve-month funding rate up fourteen basis points since October; (4) the federal SR 26-2 guidance replacing SR 11-7 as the AI model risk standard for banks; (5) Anaplan's Agentic Enterprise still not in general availability despite an October promise; (6) Truist's Q3 2026 efficiency ratio improving to fifty-four point five percent and CET1 at twelve point zero six percent; (7) the Basel III endgame still pending no final rule as of OIRA review. Let me compile both outputs carefully.
---
## Finance Pulse | Thursday, November 26, 2026
**Bottom line: October PCE landed this Thanksgiving morning and delivered a double beat that re-locks the December ninth hike -- headline at three point eight percent and core at three point three percent, the highest core reading in nearly three years -- while simultaneously cementing the multi-quarter tightening path that makes deposit re-pricing math the defining planning problem for every bank CFO heading into 2027 annual planning season; the SR 26-2 model-risk guidance that replaced SR 11-7 this past April has now become the overlooked governance requirement that is quietly restructuring how banks buy, validate, and report on AI tools inside the finance function.**
---
### Top Takeaways
1. October PCE rose three point eight percent year-over-year, up from three point six percent in September, with core prices rising three point three percent, above the three point two percent economists expected. The data print, arriving on Thanksgiving, removes any remaining ambiguity about December. 2. Kalshi prediction markets give a twenty-five basis point hike ninety-three percent odds at the December ninth meeting, with the fed funds target currently at three point seventy-five to four percent. The hold scenario that briefly opened last Tuesday has fully closed. 3. The most likely rate path now runs to a four point zero to four point twenty-five percent range after December, with the gov.house model assigning eighty-three percent probability to a hike in March 2027 as well, targeting a four point twenty-five to four point fifty percent range by that meeting. 4. Federal Reserve Supervisory Guidance SR 26-2, effective April 17, 2026, replaced SR 11-7 as the governing standard for AI and machine-learning model risk in banking, expanding coverage to generative AI systems used in decision support and operational workflows and creating new model inventory, validation, and documentation requirements. 5. Anaplan's Agentic Enterprise -- skills-based agents for the office of the CFO covering FP&A, treasury, controllership, and procurement deployed on Amazon Bedrock -- was originally promised for October 2026 and as of November 2026 had not confirmed general availability.
---
### Three Key Themes
**1. The PCE double-beat changes the 2027 annual plan (New)** Core PCE climbed three point three percent year-over-year in October, an uptick from September's three point one percent reading and the highest level in almost three years. October's monthly pace eased from September's zero point five percent gain, but core inflation did not ease at all, holding at zero point three percent for a second straight month and rising on the year. For bank CFOs in the middle of Q4 annual planning, this is not just a December data point -- it validates the multi-hike scenario through mid-2027 as the working base case, not a tail risk. The fed funds target range has been three point seventy-five to four percent since September 17, 2026, with the next decision on December 9.
**2. The deposit re-pricing squeeze is tightening in real time (Evolving)** Short- and mid-tenor funding costs have already snapped back up since the October hold, with the twelve-month funding rate rising fourteen basis points and the twenty-four-month rate rising twelve basis points between late October and mid-November. The latest FDIC industry NIM reading stood at three point thirty-two percent for Q2 2026, which predates the Fed's September hike -- meaning the deposit re-pricing pressure from the September move has not yet fully shown up in published industry data. A December hike will compound that lag further. The divergence is already visible at the cohort level: the top twenty-five performing banks posted a median NIM of four point eleven percent versus three point fifty-seven percent for the rest, funded in part by a cheaper deposit cost of one point fifty-two percent average versus one point ninety-four percent for everyone else.
**3. SR 26-2 is restructuring the AI governance purchase decision at banks (New)** This is the angle that prior episodes have not addressed. SR 26-2, effective April 17, 2026, expanded model risk management coverage to generative AI systems used in decision support and operational workflows, creating new model inventory, validation, and documentation requirements for every CFO at a financial institution. This is not aspirational regulatory language -- it is a live compliance requirement. Banks that have piloted or deployed AI tools in FP&A, treasury, or the close must now treat those tools as model-risk inventory items subject to validation and documentation. That changes the buying calculus: a bank cannot simply subscribe to a finance AI tool without establishing a governance trail. Vendors that can demonstrate documented model cards, audit logs, and validation frameworks are moving ahead in bank procurement reviews.
---
### Banking Finance-Function Metrics
Truist Bank reported total assets of five hundred forty-six point six billion at Q3 2026, with a CET1 ratio of twelve point zero six percent above regulatory requirements, an efficiency ratio of fifty-four point five three percent, and a NIM of three point thirteen percent. That efficiency ratio represents a material improvement trajectory from the fifty-seven point nine percent posted in Q1 2026, as Truist continues to process operational efficiency programs to eliminate redundant systems from its 2019 merger.
On the DFAST front, the 2026 stress test results showed Truist with a minimum CET1 of nine point seven percent in the severely adverse scenario, while KeyCorp posted seven point three percent and Regions and PNC each posted capital ratio declines that remain well above regulatory minimums. The Federal Reserve's June 2026 large bank capital requirements set the stress capital buffer for PNC, Truist, and Regions each at two point five percent above the four point five percent minimum, while KeyCorp carried a higher stress capital buffer of three point two percent.
---
### Regulatory Radar
Basel III Endgame: As of the most recent guidance, the March 2026 proposals remain pending a final rule, with the public comment period having closed on June 18, 2026, and no specific effective date yet set. Taken together with proposed changes to the Fed's stress-testing framework, the proposals would lower Common Equity Tier 1 capital requirements by four point eight percent for Category I and II firms, by five point two percent for Category III and IV firms, and by seven point eight percent for smaller banks. No material movement this week; OIRA review continues.
Category III and IV banks can choose whether to adopt the Expanded Risk-Based Approach or continue under a revised Standardized Approach, giving mid-sized regional banks more flexibility than the largest GSIBs. For super-regional finance teams, this optionality is a live capital planning variable that belongs in the 2027 planning scenario set.
---
### AI in Finance
**SR 26-2 as a purchasing filter:** The replacement of SR 11-7 with SR 26-2 this April is the most consequential structural development in bank AI governance that has received insufficient attention in transformation conversations. Every generative AI tool deployed in a bank finance function -- whether it touches FP&A forecasting, variance analysis, regulatory reporting drafts, or close automation -- now must be inventoried and validated under the new standard. This is driving a bifurcation in vendor selection: platforms that have invested in model documentation and audit-log capabilities are differentiating from those that have not.
**MCP as a live procurement threshold:** MCP is now a buying criterion, and as of November 2026, Aleph, Pigment, Cube, Planful, Datarails, Anaplan, OneStream, Vena, and Prophix all expose finance data to external AI tools through MCP. This is a confirmed market-level shift, not a vendor claim.
**Agentic AI: promise versus delivery:** As much as eighty percent of FP&A work is still spent extracting and packaging data and performing simple calculations; agentic AI is intended to move finance teams from producing reports to interpreting performance and advising the business. In one documented BCG deployment, a finance insight agent automated more than ninety percent of business intelligence work in nine months -- work that previously took three years. However, Anaplan's slip past its October general availability date for the Agentic Enterprise is a reminder that timeline promises from enterprise vendors are running ahead of delivery.
**CFO connection:** Wolters Kluwer's 2026 Future Ready CFO Report, based on responses from over sixteen hundred senior finance executives across twenty global markets, found that roughly sixty percent expect major transformational change from AI in financial modeling, reporting, capital allocation, FP&A, and scenario planning over the next three years. Banks that have not built the SR 26-2 governance infrastructure will find that expectation increasingly difficult to convert into actual deployment.
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
The October PCE print arriving on Thanksgiving creates a specific problem for bank CFOs in annual planning: core PCE prices were up three point three percent over the twelve months to October, and the underlying rate had climbed back up after its cooler stretch in the summer. Any 2027 budget built on a base case of one December hike and then plateau is now materially understated on funding costs. CFOs must layer in at minimum a March 2027 hike scenario. Bank of America's view is that the Fed wants to move slowly at a quarterly pace because it is unsure how restrictive policy is, with a terminal rate forecast at four point twenty-five to four point fifty percent staying at that level through end of 2027.
For finance transformation budget prioritization, the SR 26-2 governance requirement is creating a new line item: model validation for AI tools. Banks that purchased or piloted AI in FP&A and close in 2025 and 2026 without building that governance infrastructure are now facing retrofit costs. That is a specific finance transformation demand driver -- not just the AI tooling itself, but the control framework around it.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The consensus framing treats the deposit re-pricing squeeze as a uniform headwind across the super-regional cohort. But deposit costs behave differently depending on franchise quality, and that kind of deposit base is built, not bought off a rate sheet -- which is exactly why cost of funding, not asset yield, is where a bank can build a durable NIM advantage. A bank where thirty-five percent of total deposits sit in non-interest-bearing accounts has a massive cost advantage over a bank where that figure is twelve percent. The finance transformation implication is underappreciated: banks that have invested in deposit analytics, relationship-level pricing tools, and real-time funding cost dashboards are not just managing a current-cycle headwind -- they are building structural NIM separation that will compound if the terminal rate stays elevated through 2027. The CFO who treats deposit franchise analytics as a technology investment rather than a finance-function overhead is making a structural bet, not just a tactical one.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **"Your October PCE number came in this morning -- core at three point three percent, the highest in nearly three years. Has your 2027 plan been stress-tested against a scenario where the Fed hikes in December and again in March, with terminal rate at four point fifty?"** 2. **"SR 26-2 replaced SR 11-7 in April and now requires model inventory and validation for every generative AI tool used in decision support inside the finance function. Have you audited which of your FP&A and close tools are in scope, and do you have documented model cards for each?"** 3. **"The data shows the top-quartile banks are running deposit costs forty basis points below the peer median. Is your finance function producing real-time visibility into deposit franchise quality by relationship, segment, and channel -- or are you still managing funding costs at the aggregate balance sheet level?"**

item.title: Finance Pulse - Nov 25, 2026
item.description:
I'll run all major searches simultaneously across macro, rates, banking, regulatory, and AI-in-finance domains to capture the freshest developments as of November 25, 2026.I now have strong, sourced, fresh material across all required domains. Let me compile both outputs carefully, surfacing angles genuinely new as of November 25, 2026, and avoiding all recycled themes from prior episodes.
---
## Finance Pulse | Wednesday, November 25, 2026
**Bottom line: October PCE data -- landing today, the Wednesday before Thanksgiving -- is the single data point that will either lock or crack the December ninth twenty-five basis point consensus; simultaneously, a KBRA analysis reveals the Fed's hike cycle has re-introduced a funding-cost reversal risk that erased two years of deposit-cost progress, MCP connectivity has hardened from a differentiator into a purchasing threshold for FP&A platforms, and PNC's just-filed CFO succession and branch-rationalization data together tell a coherent operating-model story that every transformation client should hear.**
---
### Top Takeaways
1. **PCE is the fulcrum today.** The Cleveland Fed's nowcast points to core PCE at roughly three point two percent year-over-year for October. If it prints in line or hotter, the December ninth twenty-five basis point hike is locked. A softer surprise reopens the hold debate that briefly surfaced after Bessent's CBS warning last Sunday.
2. **The funding-cost reversal risk is now documented and quantified.** KBRA Financial Intelligence shows the average cost of total funding had fallen thirty-six basis points to one point eight seven percent as of the second quarter of 2026, and industry NIM had climbed to three point nine four percent -- but the September hike has begun unwinding that progress. Banks that rebuilt their NIMs on declining deposit costs are now exposed to a second repricing cycle.
3. **MCP is a buying criterion, not a feature.** As of November 2026, nine major FP&A platforms -- including Aleph, Pigment, Anaplan, OneStream, and Vena -- expose finance data through the Model Context Protocol. Banks evaluating FP&A vendors that cannot confirm MCP connectivity are making a purchase that may be obsolete within twelve months.
4. **PNC is running a dual operating-model story simultaneously.** The bank closed twenty branch locations between September and November and filed to close three more, while separately expanding its longer-term plan to more than three hundred and seventy new locations by 2031. That is network rationalization and growth investment running in parallel -- a pattern that creates direct finance-function pressure around footprint analytics, cost allocation, and capital planning.
5. **Anaplan's Agentic Enterprise has a credibility problem.** The platform announced skills-based CFO-office agents deployed on Amazon Bedrock in June, promised general availability for October, and has not confirmed a GA date as of November 2026. That slip matters for procurement teams mid-evaluation.
---
### Key Themes
**Theme 1 -- NEW: The PCE inflection and what it means for NIM planning assumptions.** Today's October PCE print arrives at exactly the moment when bank CFOs are building 2027 budgets. The Cleveland Fed's nowcast points to core PCE rising zero point two seven percent in October, which would lift the annual rate to about three point two percent. FedWatch data showed a fifty-nine point nine percent chance that rates will be fifty basis points higher by the January 2027 meeting, and a thirty-seven point six percent chance of twenty-five basis points higher. That January ambiguity -- not just December -- is the new planning problem. A CFO who locks 2027 NII assumptions to a four-to-four-twenty-five terminal rate today may need to re-plan for four-fifty to four-seventy-five as early as February.
**Theme 2 -- NEW: The funding-cost reversal documented by KBRA.** The Federal Reserve's decision to raise interest rates for the first time in more than three years, coupled with last month's rate hold, could undo a beneficial trend for U.S. banks that have enjoyed steadily declining funding and deposit costs over the past two years. KBRA data shows that the average cost of total funding fell thirty-six basis points to one point eight seven percent for the second quarter of 2026, while average NIM increased to three point nine four percent from three point five one percent in the third quarter of 2024. Shifts away from non-interest-bearing deposits toward interest-bearing accounts due to market competition stand to increase funding costs and squeeze NIM, as banks with higher balances of non-interest-bearing deposits are vulnerable to repricing pressures.
**Theme 3 -- EVOLVING: MCP as a finance-platform purchasing threshold.** MCP is now a buying criterion: as of November 2026, Aleph, Pigment, Cube, Planful, Datarails, Anaplan, OneStream, Vena, and Prophix expose finance data to external AI tools through MCP. This is no longer a future-state conversation. Banks mid-RFP for FP&A platforms should require vendors to demonstrate live MCP connectivity to their core LLM stack today, not on a roadmap.
---
### Banking Finance-Function Metrics
**NIM and deposit costs:** SOFR net interest margin rose seven basis points to one point seven eight percent, while fixed-rate NIM edged up two basis points to one point seven zero percent. Short-and mid-tenor funding rates have already moved back up, with the twelve-month rate rising fourteen basis points to four point seven three percent and the twenty-four-month rate rising twelve basis points to four point eight six percent. The funding curve is tightening before the December decision even lands.
**Commercial lending vs. consumer:** Third-quarter results from PNC, U.S. Bancorp, Truist, Fifth Third, Regions, and KeyCorp show regional banks putting AI into everyday operations, with commercial lending increasing at PNC, U.S. Bancorp, Regions, and KeyCorp. Truist noted a decline in consumer loan balances even as commercial lending increased.
**PNC operating-model signal:** PNC closed twenty branches from September twenty-fifth through November thirteenth in Arizona, Colorado, Pennsylvania, and Virginia, and is slated to close three more. PNC said in August it expected to open about fifty-five new branches in 2026, and in November expanded its longer-term plan to more than three hundred and seventy new locations by 2031.
**PNC CFO succession:** On November fifth, PNC's board appointed Alexander E. C. Overstrom, currently Executive Vice President and Head of Retail Banking, as Chief Financial Officer, effective March first, 2027. A CFO transition at a super-regional in a rising-rate environment is a transformation-spend signal: new finance leaders typically conduct operating-model reviews within their first ninety days.
**Fifth Third and Comerica:** The biggest catalyst for Fifth Third in recent history is the completed ten point nine billion dollar acquisition of Comerica, which has now created the nation's ninth-largest bank. Post-merger finance integration at that scale is a multi-year workload -- chart of accounts harmonization, intercompany eliminations, consolidated regulatory reporting -- that sustains demand for finance-platform investment.
**KeyCorp AI:** KeyCorp identified four areas for its AI work: commercial onboarding and servicing, commercial originations, consumer servicing, and software engineering, with CEO Chris Gorman naming these as the initial target domains.
**Regions productivity:** Regions reported AI-driven productivity gains of twenty percent as of its Q3 2026 earnings call, with sixteen use cases and fourteen in production.
---
### Regulatory Radar
**Basel III Endgame -- unchanged from prior coverage.** The FDIC's White House submission of November thirteenth remains the status quo; OIRA review is ongoing. The comment period on the March 2026 re-proposal closed June eighteenth, and no specific effective date has yet been set for the final rule as of the most recent guidance. Combined with proposed changes to the Fed's stress-testing framework, the proposals would lower Common Equity Tier 1 requirements by four point eight percent for Category I and II firms, five point two percent for Category III and IV firms, and seven point eight percent for smaller banks. For mid-sized regionals, the Category III/IV optionality -- the choice whether to adopt the Expanded Risk-Based Approach or continue under a revised Standardized Approach -- is a live capital-planning decision that feeds directly into 2027 budget assumptions.
**Global operational risk deadline:** India's RBI confirmed April first, 2027 as the effective date for the new Basel III Standardized Approach for minimum operational risk capital requirements for commercial banks. While U.S.-specific, this signals a global wave of operational risk capital recalibration arriving within eighteen months that will affect the reporting workload for any bank with international operations.
---
### AI in Finance
**MCP as the new procurement gate:** The shift from MCP as a differentiator to a table-stakes requirement happened in this quarter. Anaplan's Agentic Enterprise -- announced June thirtieth with skills-based agents for FP&A, treasury, controllership, and procurement deployed on Amazon Bedrock -- had an originally promised October 2026 rollout that had not been confirmed as generally available as of November 2026. That is a concrete credibility data point for procurement teams.
**LLM benchmarking for finance tasks:** Vals AI's Finance Agent benchmark tests models on the filings research an entry-level financial analyst does; as of November eleventh, Fable five point two ranks first at sixty-nine point four seven percent and Opus five point five second at sixty-seven point eight five percent. Banks that have standardized on a specific LLM for their finance-function agents should validate against this benchmark before the next contract renewal.
**Agentic AI spend control gap:** Bain's survey of one hundred and fifty CFOs in North America and Europe finds that seventy-seven percent report unexpected agentic AI costs, ninety-seven percent expect spending to increase over the next two years, and only eight percent are very confident they can see all agentic AI usage, including tools adopted without central approval. This is not a vendor marketing data point -- it is a governance and controls gap that sits squarely in the controller and CFO-office remit.
**Datarails FinanceOS and the data-layer play:** In March 2026, Datarails launched FinanceOS, its Finance Operating System, described as the governed foundation connecting financial data, business logic, workflows, applications, and AI across the Office of the CFO. Fifty-one percent of respondents in the 2026 FP&A Impact Report say the connection between their FP&A tools and source systems -- such as ERP, CRM, and HRIS -- is moderate or limited. The data-layer gap is what makes the FinanceOS framing commercially viable; it is also the reason agentic FP&A agents underperform at banks that have not addressed their core data architecture.
**OneStream's finance-specific agent architecture:** OneStream's SensibleAI Agents are finance-specific AI agents that run on the same data model, so calculations come from deterministic financial logic rather than a probabilistic language model's estimate. For bank controllers nervous about model risk in the close and consolidation process, deterministic-over-probabilistic is the right governance framing to put in front of an internal audit committee.
**CFO agenda connection:** The Bain governance gap, the Vals AI benchmark, the Anaplan GA slip, and the MCP standardization all point to the same buying-pattern signal: banks are slowing new agentic AI commitments and pivoting toward governance frameworks and integration quality. The question finance leaders are now asking vendors is not "can your agent do this?" but "how do I audit what your agent did?"
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
1. **2027 budget season is happening in the most ambiguous rate environment since the hiking cycle began.** The gov.house forward model gives a fifty-two percent chance of a January 2027 hike and an eighty-three percent chance of a March 2027 hike, implying a most-likely terminal range of four point fifty to four point seventy-five percent. CFOs building NII sensitivity tables for 2027 need to scenario-plan at least three rate paths: December only, December plus January, and December plus January plus March.
2. **The PNC CFO succession creates a window.** An incoming CFO from a retail banking background, effective March first, will want to conduct an operating-model assessment of the finance function. That is a transformation entry point.
3. **The cost-workload squeeze is intensifying.** Fifth Third's Comerica integration, PNC's branch network rebalancing, and the Truist turnaround story all create rising finance-function workloads -- more entities, more cost centers, more regulatory submissions -- against a backdrop where headcount budgets are not growing proportionally.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The data showing industry NIM recovering to three point nine four percent and funding costs declining to one point eight seven percent through mid-2026 is being treated as a durable structural improvement. It is not. KBRA's analysis makes clear that the September hike has restarted the deposit-repricing clock. The banks that cut the deepest into their CD and money-market rates during the 2024-2025 easing window are now the most exposed to the next repricing wave. The NIM recovery was partially a one-time catch-up, and CFOs who built their 2027 NII plans around sustaining that level are likely to miss.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **"Has your CFO mapped the three rate paths for 2027 NII -- December only, December-January, and December-January-March -- and stress-tested your deposit beta assumptions against each?"** The January and March hike probabilities are now material, not tail risks.
2. **"Which of your FP&A vendors have confirmed live MCP connectivity today, not on a roadmap -- and have you tested whether your agents can actually reach your ERP and core banking data through that connection?"** Fifty-one percent of finance teams report that connection is moderate or limited even after purchasing the platform.
3. **"If your incoming or current CFO were asked by internal audit to show every agentic AI workflow touching the financial close, could you produce that audit trail today?"** Only eight percent of large-company CFOs say they have full visibility into all agentic AI usage -- and that is the governance gap regulators will eventually close for them.

## Finance Pulse | Wednesday, November 25, 2026
**Bottom line: October PCE data -- landing today, the Wednesday before Thanksgiving -- is the single data point that will either lock or crack the December ninth twenty-five basis point consensus; simultaneously, a KBRA analysis reveals the Fed's hike cycle has re-introduced a funding-cost reversal risk that erased two years of deposit-cost progress, MCP connectivity has hardened from a differentiator into a purchasing threshold for FP&A platforms, and PNC's just-filed CFO succession and branch-rationalization data together tell a coherent operating-model story that every transformation client should hear.**
---
### Top Takeaways
1. **PCE is the fulcrum today.** The Cleveland Fed's nowcast points to core PCE at roughly three point two percent year-over-year for October. If it prints in line or hotter, the December ninth twenty-five basis point hike is locked. A softer surprise reopens the hold debate that briefly surfaced after Bessent's CBS warning last Sunday.
2. **The funding-cost reversal risk is now documented and quantified.** KBRA Financial Intelligence shows the average cost of total funding had fallen thirty-six basis points to one point eight seven percent as of the second quarter of 2026, and industry NIM had climbed to three point nine four percent -- but the September hike has begun unwinding that progress. Banks that rebuilt their NIMs on declining deposit costs are now exposed to a second repricing cycle.
3. **MCP is a buying criterion, not a feature.** As of November 2026, nine major FP&A platforms -- including Aleph, Pigment, Anaplan, OneStream, and Vena -- expose finance data through the Model Context Protocol. Banks evaluating FP&A vendors that cannot confirm MCP connectivity are making a purchase that may be obsolete within twelve months.
4. **PNC is running a dual operating-model story simultaneously.** The bank closed twenty branch locations between September and November and filed to close three more, while separately expanding its longer-term plan to more than three hundred and seventy new locations by 2031. That is network rationalization and growth investment running in parallel -- a pattern that creates direct finance-function pressure around footprint analytics, cost allocation, and capital planning.
5. **Anaplan's Agentic Enterprise has a credibility problem.** The platform announced skills-based CFO-office agents deployed on Amazon Bedrock in June, promised general availability for October, and has not confirmed a GA date as of November 2026. That slip matters for procurement teams mid-evaluation.

That January ambiguity -- not just December -- is the new planning problem. A CFO who locks 2027 NII assumptions to a four-to-four-twenty-five terminal rate today may need to re-plan for four-fifty to four-seventy-five as early as February.
**Theme 2 -- NEW: The funding-cost reversal documented by KBRA.** The Federal Reserve's decision to raise interest rates for the first time in more than three years, coupled with last month's rate hold, could undo a beneficial trend for U.S. banks that have enjoyed steadily declining funding and deposit costs over the past two years. KBRA data shows that the average cost of total funding fell thirty-six basis points to one point eight seven percent for the second quarter of 2026, while average NIM increased to three point nine four percent from three point five one percent in the third quarter of 2024. Shifts away from non-interest-bearing deposits toward interest-bearing accounts due to market competition stand to increase funding costs and squeeze NIM, as banks with higher balances of non-interest-bearing deposits are vulnerable to repricing pressures.
**Theme 3 -- EVOLVING: MCP as a finance-platform purchasing threshold.** MCP is now a buying criterion: as of November 2026, Aleph, Pigment, Cube, Planful, Datarails, Anaplan, OneStream, Vena, and Prophix expose finance data to external AI tools through MCP. ---
### Banking Finance-Function Metrics
**NIM and deposit costs:** SOFR net interest margin rose seven basis points to one point seven eight percent, while fixed-rate NIM edged up two basis points to one point seven zero percent. Short-and mid-tenor funding rates have already moved back up, with the twelve-month rate rising fourteen basis points to four point seven three percent and the twenty-four-month rate rising twelve basis points to four point eight six percent. The funding curve is tightening before the December decision even lands.
**Commercial lending vs. consumer:** Third-quarter results from PNC, U.S. Bancorp, Truist, Fifth Third, Regions, and KeyCorp show regional banks putting AI into everyday operations, with commercial lending increasing at PNC, U.S. Bancorp, Regions, and KeyCorp. Truist noted a decline in consumer loan balances even as commercial lending increased.
**PNC operating-model signal:** PNC closed twenty branches from September twenty-fifth through November thirteenth in Arizona, Colorado, Pennsylvania, and Virginia, and is slated to close three more. item.description:
## Finance Pulse | Tuesday, November 24, 2026
**Bottom line: Treasury Secretary Bessent's Sunday overtightening warning on CBS, arriving simultaneously with a sharp equity rout, has introduced a genuine hold scenario for December ninth for the first time since October -- with CME hold odds jumping from near-zero to eleven percent in a single day -- creating a fork-in-the-road planning problem for bank CFOs that is more complex than the previous "hike is certain" consensus; meanwhile a Bain survey published yesterday reveals that seventy-seven percent of CFOs are absorbing unexpected agentic AI costs they cannot fully track, and Baird's simultaneous upgrade of Citizens and Truist to outperform identifies two super-regional turnaround stories the finance transformation market should watch.**
---
### Top Takeaways
1. The Bessent-Fed fault line is new and materially changes the December planning assumption: a hold is now a live scenario, not a tail risk. 2. Agentic AI spend is outpacing CFO financial controls -- a Bain survey of one hundred fifty large-company CFOs published November twenty-third is the most important governance data point of the week. 3. Baird upgraded both Citizens and Truist to outperform simultaneously, flagging divergent recovery trajectories in the super-regional cohort. 4. The ten-year Treasury yield crossed four point nine two percent, compressing unrealized losses in bank hold-to-maturity portfolios and raising new duration-management pressure. 5. The Basel III Endgame OIRA package is at White House review -- no new movement since November thirteenth, but the finalization clock is ticking toward published rulemaking.
---
### Key Themes
**1. The Bessent Intervention: A Genuine Hold Signal (New)**
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned Sunday that the Federal Reserve risks jeopardizing the US economy by overtightening in response to the latest inflation data, pointing to signs of fragility in the financial system. The warning, delivered on CBS Face the Nation, is not an isolated comment: it continues an argument Bessent has made throughout November, having warned on November thirteenth that it would be a mistake to hike aggressively into an energy supply shock he said was already easing, and again on November twentieth urging policymakers not to back a larger rate rise. The political backdrop deepened further: President Trump has repeatedly pushed the Fed to lower interest rates, while Bill Ackman warned on X that the Fed is "about to make another mistake," arguing that three percent is a more realistic inflation target in a world of higher military spending, protectionism, and AI infrastructure investment.
The market reaction is what makes this actionable for CFOs. The odds of no December hike jumped from zero to about eleven percent in a single day, with CME FedWatch showing hold odds at eleven point four percent and hike odds at eighty-eight point six percent. That is a materially different planning environment than Monday. The Fed's range remains three point seven-five to four percent after the September hike, while the two-year Treasury yield has risen from three point four-seven percent on January second to four point sixty-three percent on November twentieth -- a one point one-six percentage-point climb in 2026.
**2. Agentic AI Cost Governance: The CFO Blind Spot (New)**
A Bain and Company survey of one hundred fifty CFOs and senior finance leaders at large companies in North America and Europe, published November twenty-third, finds that seventy-seven percent report unexpected agentic AI costs, yet only seventeen percent are very or extremely concerned about controlling that spending. The complacency gap is striking: ninety-seven percent of respondents expect agentic AI spending to increase over the next two years, and sixty-six percent anticipate spending growth of at least twenty-five percent, yet only eight percent are very confident they can see all agentic AI usage, including tools adopted without central approval. The ROI picture is mixed: sixty-one percent of respondents piloting or deploying agents say returns have met or exceeded expectations, while twenty-three percent report falling short.
**3. Super-Regional Bifurcation: Upgrade Signals and CRE Stress (Evolving)**
Citizens and Truist each gained more than two percent after Baird upgraded both regional banks to outperform from neutral. This is notable because the two names represent opposite recovery profiles. Super-regional banks reported commercial loan growth and higher net interest income in Q2 2026, with net interest income rising sequentially at all eleven banks, Citizens and PNC each up four percent. However, the CRE story remains uneven: commercial real estate performance diverged, with Citizens reducing its CRE charge-off rate to zero point three-six percent from zero point sixty-four percent, while Truist, US Bancorp, and KeyCorp each recorded higher CRE nonperforming assets despite overall charge-off declines, suggesting uneven stress from legacy office and multifamily exposure.
---
### Banking Finance-Function Metrics
The rate environment is forcing a split in NIM trajectory between banks with asset-sensitive books benefiting from repricing and those still absorbing elevated deposit costs. The long-end move matters separately: the ten-year Treasury yield reached four point nine-two percent as of November twentieth, which creates mark-to-market pressure on available-for-sale portfolios and complicates ALM hedging assumptions heading into year-end close.
On capital structure, PNC's board appointed Alexander Overstrom, currently Executive Vice President and Head of Retail Banking, to be Chief Financial Officer effective March first, twenty-twenty-seven, following a November fifth announcement. PNC finished Q2 with a CET1 of nine point nine percent, and lifted its quarterly common dividend eighteen percent to two dollars per share. Truist carries the highest net charge-off ratio of the three peer banks at zero point sixty-one percent and trades near book value at a price-to-earnings of twelve, with its dividend frozen since twenty-twenty-two.
---
### Regulatory Radar
The Basel III Endgame package is at OIRA. The FDIC sent revised Basel III endgame capital rules to the White House for review on November thirteenth, and the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs lists the package as a final rule awaiting review in its regulatory tracking system. Taken together with proposed changes to the Federal Reserve's stress-testing framework, the proposals would lower Common Equity Tier 1 capital requirements by four point eight percent for the largest Category I and II firms, by five point two percent for Category III and IV firms, and by seven point eight percent for smaller banks. Category III and IV banks can choose whether to adopt the new Expanded Risk-Based Approach or continue under a revised Standardised Approach, giving mid-sized regional banks more flexibility than the largest GSIBs. No new movement since November thirteenth; this is a watch item, not a decision item.
---
### AI in Finance
The Bain governance finding (covered in the Banking Finance-Function section above) is the headline. Below it, the vendor landscape is clarifying:
Anaplan announced skills-based agents for the office of the CFO covering FP&A, treasury, controllership, and procurement, deployed on Amazon Bedrock. As of November 2026, MCP has become a buying criterion, with Aleph, Pigment, Cube, Planful, Datarails, Anaplan, OneStream, Vena, and Prophix all exposing finance data to external AI tools through the protocol. Anaplan's Agentic Enterprise was announced June thirtieth, twenty-twenty-six; as of November twenty-twenty-six it had not confirmed general availability, having originally targeted October. This is the clearest current example of the gap between vendor announcement and actual deployment that bank technology buyers must assess rigorously.
OneStream's SensibleAI Agents are finance-specific agents that run on the same data model, so calculations come from deterministic financial logic rather than a probabilistic language model's estimate -- a distinction that matters acutely for bank regulatory reporting and stress-test submissions where model auditability is non-negotiable.
By mid-2026, AI in financial planning and analysis has moved from pilot projects to standard operating procedure, with McKinsey's 2026 research showing the shift concentrated in driver-based forecasting, variance analysis, scenario planning, reporting automation, and agentic processes where AI systems execute multi-step tasks with limited supervision.
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
The Bessent intervention introduces a scenario-planning imperative that goes beyond rates. A bank CFO must now carry two December scenarios simultaneously: a hike to four to four point twenty-five percent that extends the NIM tailwind but pressures credit, and a hold that freezes the tailwind but potentially stabilizes equity portfolios and unrealized losses. That is a live FP&A use case for agentic scenario modeling today.
The PNC CFO transition -- Overstrom takes over March first from a retail banking background -- is a signal that balance-sheet and funding-economics fluency is the premium skill set for the super-regional CFO role in this rate environment.
The Bain finding that only eight percent of CFOs can see all agentic AI usage creates a direct finance transformation demand signal: banks need governed, permissioned AI platforms, not shadow tool adoption. This is where the MCP standard, OneStream's deterministic agent architecture, and BlackLine's AIUC-1 governance work (covered in earlier episodes) are converging into a coherent buying thesis.
Finance planning teams are deploying agentic systems that compress forecast cycles from weeks to hours, with organizations reporting that finance teams using agentic FP&A tools can spend seventy percent of their time on analysis and decision support rather than data preparation.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The consensus framing is that higher rates are good for bank NIM and therefore good for bank finance. But the Bessent warning introduces the scenario that the Fed's December hike, if it materializes, could be the hike that breaks something -- not because of the twenty-five basis points itself, but because Wall Street is in correction territory and the Treasury is now openly stating that the greater risk to the economy comes from the Fed rather than the energy shock. A CFO who has built a 2027 budget on a continued NIM expansion story should stress-test the hold-then-cut scenario, which has not been part of any bank planning conversation this quarter.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **The Bessent-Fed divergence as a planning scenario**: Has your bank built a 2027 budget that isolates the hold-then-cut path, or does every scenario assume the multi-hike path? The hold odds just moved from zero to eleven percent in a day -- that is now a scenario that requires explicit modeling.
2. **Agentic AI spend governance**: The Bain finding that seventy-seven percent of large-company CFOs are absorbing unexpected agentic AI costs they cannot track is a direct audit and controls gap. For bank clients, where model risk and regulatory scrutiny apply to AI, this is not a minor issue -- it is a governance program waiting to be built.
3. **CRE divergence within the super-regional cohort**: Citizens' CRE charge-off rate fell from zero point sixty-four to zero point thirty-six percent while Truist, US Bancorp, and KeyCorp saw nonperforming CRE assets rise. The same rate environment is producing opposite credit outcomes across the peer group -- which creates a data-driven conversation about whether your client's provisioning and allowance methodology is appropriately differentiated.

Truist carries the highest net charge-off ratio of the three peer banks at zero point sixty-one percent and trades near book value at a price-to-earnings of twelve, with its dividend frozen since twenty-twenty-two.
---
### Regulatory Radar
The Basel III Endgame package is at OIRA. The FDIC sent revised Basel III endgame capital rules to the White House for review on November thirteenth, and the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs lists the package as a final rule awaiting review in its regulatory tracking system. Taken together with proposed changes to the Federal Reserve's stress-testing framework, the proposals would lower Common Equity Tier 1 capital requirements by four point eight percent for the largest Category I and II firms, by five point two percent for Category III and IV firms, and by seven point eight percent for smaller banks. Category III and IV banks can choose whether to adopt the new Expanded Risk-Based Approach or continue under a revised Standardised Approach, giving mid-sized regional banks more flexibility than the largest GSIBs. No new movement since November thirteenth; this is a watch item, not a decision item.
---
### AI in Finance
The Bain governance finding (covered in the Banking Finance-Function section above) is the headline. Below it, the vendor landscape is clarifying:
Anaplan announced skills-based agents for the office of the CFO covering FP&A, treasury, controllership, and procurement, deployed on Amazon Bedrock. As of November 2026, MCP has become a buying criterion, with Aleph, Pigment, Cube, Planful, Datarails, Anaplan, OneStream, Vena, and Prophix all exposing finance data to external AI tools through the protocol. Anaplan's Agentic Enterprise was announced June thirtieth, twenty-twenty-six; as of November twenty-twenty-six it had not confirmed general availability, having originally targeted October. This is the clearest current example of the gap between vendor announcement and actual deployment that bank technology buyers must assess rigorously.
OneStream's SensibleAI Agents are finance-specific agents that run on the same data model, so calculations come from deterministic financial logic rather than a probabilistic language model's estimate -- a distinction that matters acutely for bank regulatory reporting and stress-test submissions where model auditability is non-negotiable.
By mid-2026, AI in financial planning and analysis has moved from pilot projects to standard operating procedure, with McKinsey's 2026 research showing the shift concentrated in driver-based forecasting, variance analysis, scenario planning, reporting automation, and agentic processes where AI systems execute multi-step tasks with limited supervision.
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
The Bessent intervention introduces a scenario-planning imperative that goes beyond rates. A bank CFO must now carry two December scenarios simultaneously: a hike to four to four point twenty-five percent that extends the NIM tailwind but pressures credit, and a hold that freezes the tailwind but potentially stabilizes equity portfolios and unrealized losses. That is a live FP&A use case for agentic scenario modeling today.
The PNC CFO transition -- Overstrom takes over March first from a retail banking background -- is a signal that balance-sheet and funding-economics fluency is the premium skill set for the super-regional CFO role in this rate environment.
The Bain finding that only eight percent of CFOs can see all agentic AI usage creates a direct finance transformation demand signal: banks need governed, permissioned AI platforms, not shadow tool adoption. This is where the MCP standard, OneStream's deterministic agent architecture, and BlackLine's AIUC-1 governance work (covered in earlier episodes) are converging into a coherent buying thesis.
Finance planning teams are deploying agentic systems that compress forecast cycles from weeks to hours, with organizations reporting that finance teams using agentic FP&A tools can spend seventy percent of their time on analysis and decision support rather than data preparation.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The consensus framing is that higher rates are good for bank NIM and therefore good for bank finance. But the Bessent warning introduces the scenario that the Fed's December hike, if it materializes, could be the hike that breaks something -- not because of the twenty-five basis points itself, but because Wall Street is in correction territory and the Treasury is now openly stating that the greater risk to the economy comes from the Fed rather than the energy shock. A CFO who has built a 2027 budget on a continued NIM expansion story should stress-test the hold-then-cut scenario, which has not been part of any bank planning conversation this quarter.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **The Bessent-Fed divergence as a planning scenario**: Has your bank built a 2027 budget that isolates the hold-then-cut path, or does every scenario assume the multi-hike path? The hold odds just moved from zero to eleven percent in a day -- that is now a scenario that requires explicit modeling.
2. **Agentic AI spend governance**: The Bain finding that seventy-seven percent of large-company CFOs are absorbing unexpected agentic AI costs they cannot track is a direct audit and controls gap. For bank clients, where model risk and regulatory scrutiny apply to AI, this is not a minor issue -- it is a governance program waiting to be built.
3. **CRE divergence within the super-regional cohort**: Citizens' CRE charge-off rate fell from zero point sixty-four to zero point thirty-six percent while Truist, US Bancorp, and KeyCorp saw nonperforming CRE assets rise. The same rate environment is producing opposite credit outcomes across the peer group -- which creates a data-driven conversation about whether your client's provisioning and allowance methodology is appropriately differentiated.

item.title: Finance Pulse - Nov 23, 2026
item.description:
I now have comprehensive, fresh, sourced material for today's briefing. Let me compile both outputs carefully, ensuring no recycling of prior episode themes and surfacing genuinely new angles.
---
## Finance Pulse | Monday, November 23, 2026
**Bottom line: JPMorgan's weekend revision to three consecutive Fed hikes through March 2027, joined by Bank of America and Deutsche Bank, moves the planning horizon for bank CFOs from a December event to a multi-quarter tightening cycle with a terminal rate of four point fifty to four point seventy-five percent -- a materially different balance-sheet and budgeting assumption than even last week -- while two new cohort-level signals demand attention: Citizens Financial's J.P. Morgan conference positioning as a two hundred billion dollar-plus super-regional targeting sixteen to eighteen percent ROTCE, and PNC's post-FirstBank Colorado integration data revealing the deposit market share cost of absorbing a large acquisition.**
---
### Top Takeaways
1. **Wall Street's hike consensus just widened its runway.** JPMorgan, BofA, and Deutsche Bank all now forecast hikes in December, January, and March. Goldman Sachs and UBS expect a shorter path. CFOs cannot build a single-scenario 2027 plan; they need a range anchored at four point fifty percent, with tail risk at four point seventy-five.
2. **Citizens Financial planted a strategic flag on Friday.** CEO Bruce Van Saun described the bank as a super-regional with more than two hundred billion in assets and a sixteen to eighteen percent ROTCE target. That is a capital and returns framing, not a growth story, and it signals where finance-function investment priorities are headed at a bank still closing its transformation gap.
3. **PNC's FirstBank Colorado integration is now one year in -- and the deposit share data is sobering.** FDIC June data shows PNC's combined market share in Colorado counties came in below the pre-deal combined footprint of PNC plus FirstBank, raising a pointed question about integration economics that every CFO modeling an acquisition synergy case should study.
4. **Basel III Endgame is at OIRA but not finalized.** The comment period on the March 2026 re-proposal closed June eighteenth, and no final rule exists as of today. The White House review process is live. This limbo is now the regulatory planning constraint, not the rule itself.
5. **MCP is now a live FP&A procurement filter.** As of November 2026, nine major platforms -- including OneStream, Anaplan, Vena, Pigment, and Planful -- expose finance data via the Model Context Protocol. Banks sourcing FP&A infrastructure are now asking vendors to demonstrate MCP conformance as a condition of evaluation.
---
### Key Themes
**Theme 1 (New): The three-hike consensus reshapes CFO planning geometry.** Prior episodes covered the Waller-Williams fault line and the December decision as a binary. What is new today is that JPMorgan has formally abandoned its "December and done" call, and three major Wall Street houses now align on hikes through March 2027 with a terminal rate nearly seventy-five basis points above current levels. JPMorgan has dropped its "December and done" view, now expecting three straight hikes, with the Fed delivering twenty-five basis point increases in December, January, and March, taking rates to four point fifty to four point seventy-five percent. The firm says sticky inflation, not jobs, is the driver, and that hikes protect credibility as the Fed lacks a convincing case to pause next year. Deutsche Bank and Bank of America also forecast hikes at three straight meetings, while Goldman Sachs and UBS expect a shorter path after December. For a bank CFO, this is the moment to stress-test a "higher for longer" scenario that runs eighteen months, not six. NII models, funding cost curves, and AOCI marks all need refreshing against a four point seventy-five percent ceiling.
**Theme 2 (New): Citizens Financial's conference positioning and the super-regional aspiration premium.** Citizens Financial Group said at the J.P. Morgan European Financials Conference on November twentieth that it has moved well beyond its post-IPO turnaround and is now focused on organic growth, technology upgrades, and capital discipline, while also pointing to execution risks tied to loan volatility and the still-evolving use of AI in banking. CEO Bruce Van Saun said Citizens has evolved into a super-regional bank with more than two hundred billion in assets and a target return on tangible common equity of sixteen to eighteen percent. That ROTCE target, in a rising rate environment, is a finance-function performance statement. Getting there requires efficiency gains that only come through process automation and headcount discipline -- classic transformation demand signals.
**Theme 3 (Evolving): PNC's Colorado integration exposes the deposit share cost of M&A, a live CFO modeling lesson.** PNC's acquisition of FirstBank of Colorado, the state's largest locally owned bank, closed in January 2026, and Pittsburgh-based PNC began the process of merging the two institutions. According to the FDIC's Deposit Market Share report for June 30, 2026, PNC's market share in Boulder, Larimer, and Weld counties declined from a year earlier compared with the combined 2025 market share of PNC and FirstBank, even as PNC now holds roughly one hundred branches in Colorado and closed fourteen overlapping locations. This is an underreported integration friction point: deposit attrition during system conversion erodes the pro-forma economics. The finance transformation implication is direct -- integration-driven demand for unified data platforms, faster close cycles, and real-time deposit monitoring is not theoretical.
---
### Banking Finance-Function Metrics
**NIM and the three-hike scenario:** Super-regional banks reported commercial loan growth and higher net interest income in Q2 2026, with net interest income rising sequentially at all eleven banks, Citizens and PNC each up four percent. That Q2 momentum was modeled against a one-hike assumption. A three-hike path to four point seventy-five percent restructures liability repricing math materially for Q3 and Q4 2027.
**CRE credit divergence persists:** Commercial real estate performance diverged across the cohort: Citizens reduced its CRE charge-off rate to zero point thirty-six percent from zero point sixty-four percent, and PNC cut nonperforming CRE balances by ten percent, while Truist, U.S. Bancorp, and KeyCorp each recorded higher CRE nonperforming assets despite overall charge-off declines, suggesting uneven stress from legacy office and multifamily exposure.
**Capital markets debt activity:** First Citizens BancShares issued one point twenty-five billion dollars in notes on November nineteenth, comprising seven hundred fifty million dollars of six point seventeen percent fixed-to-floating senior notes due 2030 and five hundred million dollars of seven point eighteen percent fixed-rate reset subordinated notes due 2036. At those coupons, the blended funding cost of this issuance is a data point for treasury teams modeling their own debt stack in a rising-rate environment.
**Truist leadership transition context:** Truist announced Michael P. Lyons as incoming CEO in June 2026, with Lyons succeeding Bill Rogers. Lyons comes from PNC, where he led all lines of business and helped lead more than fifteen billion dollars of strategic acquisitions. A new CEO with a PNC operational pedigree arriving at a bank still executing its strategic reset creates specific finance-function pressure around performance reporting, capital allocation frameworks, and cost discipline.
---
### Regulatory Radar
**Basel III Endgame -- the limbo is now the story.** Prior episodes covered the OIRA submission. What is new this week is the significance of the unresolved timing: as of the most recent guidance, the Basel III Endgame is not finalized; the public comment period closed on June eighteenth, 2026, and no specific effective date has yet been set for the final rule. Taken together with proposed changes to the Federal Reserve's stress-testing framework, the proposals would lower Common Equity Tier 1 capital requirements by four point eight percent for Category I and II firms, by five point two percent for Category III and IV firms, and by seven point eight percent for smaller banks. For the super-regional cohort, specifically Category III and IV institutions, they can choose whether to adopt the Expanded Risk-Based Approach or continue under a revised Standardized Approach, giving mid-sized regional banks more flexibility than the largest GSIBs. The choice architecture is itself a strategic and finance-function decision requiring scenario modeling.
**AOCI phase-in is a sleeper provision:** the proposal would require Category III and IV banking organizations to recognize certain elements of Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income in CET1 capital, subject to a five-year phase-in beginning with the effective date of any final rule. With long-end rates rising under the three-hike scenario, this provision's materiality increases sharply. Controllers and treasury teams should be running AOCI sensitivity now, not after a final rule.
---
### AI in Finance
**The MCP standard is now a purchase-order filter, not a roadmap item.** This is the most operationally significant AI development this week. As of November 2026, MCP is now a buying criterion, with Aleph, Pigment, Cube, Planful, Datarails, Anaplan, OneStream, Vena, and Prophix all exposing finance data to external AI tools through MCP. Banks evaluating FP&A platform replacements or upgrades should add MCP conformance to their RFP scoring rubrics today.
**Anaplan's Agentic Enterprise is slipping.** Anaplan's Agentic Enterprise, announced June thirtieth, 2026, promised skills-based agents for FP&A, treasury, controllership, and procurement deployed on Amazon Bedrock, with a rollout originally targeted for October 2026; as of November 2026, Anaplan had not confirmed general availability. This is a real signal for procurement teams: announced AI roadmaps and actual GA dates are diverging. Banks negotiating multi-year platform contracts should tie milestone payments to confirmed GA, not announcement dates.
**A new entrant attempts to productize the FP&A narrative layer.** On November twentieth, Finstory, Inc. launched finstory.ai with Reeve, described as a digital employee that works like an FP&A manager, telling the "why" behind every number. Finance teams want AI, but few trust it with the numbers -- Reeve pulls the month's actuals, spots the variances, and drafts the board story page by page. This vendor occupies the narrative automation niche below the enterprise platforms. For large banks, this is not a purchasing signal yet, but it marks the direction of travel: AI-generated variance commentary is becoming a commodity, which shifts human FP&A value toward judgment and challenge.
**BCG's deployment benchmark remains the most credible ROI anchor.** BCG finds that as much as eighty percent of FP&A work is still spent extracting and packaging data and performing simple calculations, and that agentic AI will move finance teams from producing reports to interpreting performance and advising the business. In one named deployment, a finance insight agent automated more than ninety percent of business intelligence work in nine months -- work that used to take three years. CFO conversations should lead with this benchmark, not vendor marketing.
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
**The three-hike scenario is a 2027 budget re-opener.** Banks that submitted 2027 operating plans in October based on a December-and-done assumption now face a material planning error. CFOs need a formal mid-cycle reforecast triggered by the JPMorgan-BofA-Deutsche Bank consensus, covering NII sensitivity, funding cost curves, and capital allocation sequencing under a four point seventy-five percent ceiling.
**Integration economics need a finance-function owner.** The PNC-FirstBank Colorado deposit share data makes the case that M&A integration requires real-time finance infrastructure: unified data models, faster customer analytics, and deposit retention dashboards. Banks planning or executing integrations -- and Fifth Third absorbed Comerica, Huntington added Veritex and Cadence, and PNC acquired FirstBank of Colorado during this cycle -- are creating transformation demand that is structural, not discretionary.
**The ROTCE race is a finance-function performance statement.** Citizens' sixteen to eighteen percent target, against a rising-rate backdrop, requires the finance function to deliver not just reporting but actionable cost intelligence. That means FP&A platforms with driver-based models, treasury systems that model funding costs dynamically, and controllership automation that reduces close time to redirect headcount to analysis.
**AI governance is the new procurement gate.** Citizens specifically pointed to execution risks tied to the still-evolving use of artificial intelligence in banking at a major investor conference. When a super-regional CEO names AI governance as an execution risk in a public forum, it signals that AI governance is moving from a risk function concern to a CFO-level accountability. Finance transformation programs that include AI tools need an explicit governance layer to get board approval.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The three-hike consensus from JPMorgan, BofA, and Deutsche Bank may be doing bank CFOs a disservice if it crowds out scenario planning. Goldman Sachs and UBS expect a shorter path after December, and JPMorgan itself notes that Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has left the policy path without an overarching narrative, meaning decisions will be more data-dependent, not less. A CFO who plans against a single-path hike consensus and then faces a data surprise -- a soft PCE, a labor market inflection -- will be caught in a re-plan cycle. The more durable planning discipline is a range: a base case at four point fifty percent, a bull case at four point twenty-five, and a tail case at four point seventy-five, with pre-built triggers for each.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **"Your 2027 operating plan was probably built on a one-hike assumption. JPMorgan, BofA, and Deutsche Bank now say three hikes through March. What does your NII model look like at four point seventy-five percent, and have you re-opened the budget?"**
2. **"The PNC-FirstBank Colorado data shows deposit share fell below the pre-deal combined footprint six months post-close. If you're modeling acquisition synergies right now, what does your finance infrastructure actually give you in terms of real-time deposit retention visibility?"**
3. **"Nine major FP&A platforms now support MCP as of this month. If you're in a platform evaluation or renewal cycle, is MCP conformance in your RFP? And do you have a contract clause tied to confirmed GA rather than vendor roadmap promises -- given Anaplan's Agentic Enterprise still hasn't reached general availability three months after its promised October launch?"**

---
## Finance Pulse | Friday, November 20, 2026
**Bottom line: The Waller-Williams fault line is now the Fed's defining internal drama heading into December ninth -- Waller on Wednesday doubled down on fifty basis points and introduced a wholly new framing: a twenty-five basis point hike only works if it delivers a credible January signal, and if the Fed cannot communicate that signal clearly, fifty is the cleaner choice; Williams pushed back sharply on Tuesday; meanwhile BlackLine's new AIUC-1 certification and a fresh BCG agentic-FP&A data point move the AI-in-finance story from vendor promise to governance benchmark and documented ROI -- and that combination should drive finance budget conversations at every bank CFO table today.**
---
### Top Takeaways
1. Waller escalated his December position on Wednesday with a new conditional logic: twenty-five basis points is acceptable only if a credible January forward signal is delivered; without it, fifty is preferable. That is a materially different framing than his November eighteenth position. 2. Williams drew a hard counter-line on Tuesday, explicitly ruling out "dramatic action" and naming AI infrastructure investment as the most likely persistent inflation driver -- a new analytical frame with direct relevance to bank balance sheet planning. 3. BlackLine on November eighteenth became the first agentic financial operations platform to achieve AIUC-1 certification, a runtime AI governance benchmark that goes beyond ISO 42001 and directly addresses bank examiners' model-risk demands under SR 26-2. 4. Anaplan's CFO-office agents, promised for October, have no confirmed general availability as of this week -- a concrete data point separating vendor marketing from live deployment that finance transformation buyers need. 5. Truist's consumer-bank chief, Donta Wilson, is departing and the bank is selling seven point seven billion dollars of consumer loans to Carlyle -- a portfolio restructuring signal worth watching for its provisioning and capital allocation implications. 6. The Basel III package at OIRA now carries an explicit CET1 reduction estimate: four point eight percent for Category I and II banks, five point two percent for Category III and IV, and seven point eight percent for smaller banks -- numbers not widely circulated before this week.
---
### Key Themes
**Theme 1 (Evolving): The Fifty-Basis-Point Scenario Has Grown More Structurally Complex** This is not simply "will it be fifty or twenty-five." Waller has introduced a decision-tree logic: the size of December's move is now coupled to the credibility of January forward guidance. For CFOs modeling deposit repricing and funding costs, this matters. A twenty-five basis point December move paired with an explicit January commitment produces the same twelve-month rate path as a single fifty-basis-point move -- but the deposit-beta dynamics and term-funding strategies diverge meaningfully between those two paths.
**Theme 2 (New): AI Governance Has Acquired a Certifiable Standard** BlackLine's AIUC-1 certification, achieved November eighteenth, is the first runtime AI governance credential for a finance platform. This is distinct from ISO 42001, which validates management systems. AIUC-1 certifies product resilience and adversarial robustness -- directly relevant to bank examiners applying SR 26-2 model-risk standards to agentic finance tools. This is no longer a soft differentiator; it is a procurement criterion.
**Theme 3 (New): Commercial Loan Growth Is Masking a Consumer Softening Across the Super-Regional Cohort** Across PNC, KeyCorp, U.S. Bancorp, Truist, Fifth Third, and Regions, Q3 results showed commercial and industrial lending carrying the growth load while consumer balances and consumer fee income softened. Truist is now actively restructuring the consumer book by selling seven point seven billion dollars of consumer loans. This bifurcation reshapes provisioning assumptions, NIM mix, and capital allocation priorities for Q4 planning.
---
### Banking Finance-Function Metrics
FDIC-insured institutions reported an aggregate NIM of three point three one percent in Q1 2026, eight basis points below the prior quarter, as asset yields fell faster than funding costs. The funding curve has since snapped back. As of November eleventh, the twelve-month funding rate had risen fourteen basis points to four point seven three percent and the twenty-four-month rate had risen twelve basis points to four point eight six percent.
First-quarter earnings from PNC, KeyCorp, U.S. Bancorp, Truist, Fifth Third, and Regions showed commercial lending gaining momentum and fee-based businesses carrying more weight. Corporate clients are borrowing more actively and drawing further on existing credit lines. The consumer picture is real, but not the one driving results.
Truist is now acting on that consumer weakness structurally. Truist's consumer-bank chief Donta Wilson is leaving the bank, which is also selling seven point seven billion dollars of consumer loans to Carlyle.
On the deposit side, the top twenty-five performing banks in the most recent cohort analysis posted a median NIM of four point one one percent versus three point five seven percent for the rest, funded in part by cheaper deposits at an average cost of one point five two percent for the top banks versus one point nine four percent for everyone else. The gap underscores that deposit franchise quality, not asset yield, is the primary NIM differentiator.
---
### Regulatory Radar
Basel III Endgame is at OIRA and moving. The OCC, Federal Reserve, and FDIC proposed a major overhaul of bank capital requirements in March. The OCC has submitted the rulemaking to OMB for review, and the FDIC has submitted its rulemaking simultaneously. No timeline was given for when OMB may complete the reviews.
The proposals would lower Common Equity Tier 1 capital requirements by four point eight percent for the largest banks (Category I and II); by five point two percent for Category III and IV firms; and by seven point eight percent for smaller banks. These are the first published, agency-sourced CET1 relief estimates in the current proposal cycle.
Category III and IV banks can choose whether to adopt the Expanded Risk-Based Approach or continue under a revised Standardized Approach, giving mid-sized regional banks more flexibility than the largest GSIBs. For super-regional CFOs, that optionality is a live planning decision requiring scenario modeling now.
---
### AI in Finance
**BlackLine's governance week.** BlackLine on November eighteenth became the first agentic financial operations platform to achieve AIUC-1 certification. While ISO 42001 validates enterprise AI management systems, AIUC-1 certifies runtime execution and product resilience. BlackLine subjected its Verity AI to thousands of adversarial evaluations and committed to quarterly retesting. For bank finance functions governed by SR 26-2, this is not marketing -- it is a model-risk management data point.
The move highlights the growing role of agentic AI in transforming finance operations, particularly in financial close, reconciliations, risk forecasting, and exception management. By integrating OpenAI's frontier models, BlackLine aims to enable AI agents that analyze financial data, identify anomalies, and carry out finance-related tasks at scale.
**Separating real from promised.** Anaplan's CFO-office agents, announced June thirtieth with an original October availability promise, had no confirmed general availability as of November 2026. By contrast, Workday extended Decision Intelligence to its HCM and Financials customers in October 2026.
**The ROI evidence is building.** As much as eighty percent of FP&A work is still spent extracting and packaging data and performing simple calculations. Agentic AI will move finance teams from producing reports to interpreting performance and advising the business. In one BCG-documented deployment, a finance insight agent automated more than ninety percent of business intelligence work in nine months. That used to take three years.
**SR 26-2 as a forcing function.** US Federal SR 26-2, effective April seventeenth, 2026, replaces SR 11-7 as the governing standard for AI and ML model risk in banking, expanding coverage to generative AI systems used in decision support and operational workflows and creating new model inventory, validation, and documentation requirements for every CFO at a financial institution.
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
**PNC's hospitality wager against AI.** As AI-generated advice proliferates, PNC's investments in hospitality training for employees will "be worth ten times a year from now," an executive said. PNC has broadened its branch expansion plans, adding about fifty-three locations across eight markets in South Carolina and Georgia, plus ten more in Texas, Florida, and North Carolina. This is a direct operating-model bet: human relationship density as a moat against digital commoditization -- and it carries cost and efficiency ratio implications for the CFO.
**Williams names AI as the persistent inflation driver.** New York Fed President Williams identified AI as the most likely "persistent" factor of inflation, adding that how many rate hikes and at what pace will depend on what is happening in AI. For bank CFOs, this is a new planning variable: the very technology transforming the finance function is now a named driver of the rate environment that determines NIM.
**The funding-curve repricing math for CFOs.** Bank of America now expects the Federal Reserve to hike rates twice more, in December 2026 and March 2027. BofA kept its terminal rate forecast at four point two five to four point five percent and expects rates to stay at that level through the end of 2027. That is the multi-year high-rate assumption bank CFOs must now build into 2027 and 2028 planning models.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The Basel III CET1 relief numbers -- four point eight percent for the largest banks, seven point eight percent for smaller banks -- are being read as a gift. They should not be. Capital relief without a clear OIRA completion timeline creates optionality that cannot yet be deployed. Banks that pre-emptively restructure balance sheets, expand lending, or accelerate M&A based on projected capital relief before the rule is final are taking planning risk that the finance function should be explicitly flagging, not enabling.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **The Waller decision-tree question**: Ask your client whether their December rate planning scenario separates the twenty-five-plus-January-signal path from the fifty-in-December path -- because the deposit repricing, term-funding hedging, and NIM trajectory differ between the two even if the twelve-month rate level converges.
2. **AIUC-1 as a procurement filter**: BlackLine is now the only agentic finance platform with a certified runtime AI governance credential. Ask your client's transformation team whether their AI vendor evaluation criteria include any post-ISO-42001 governance standard -- and whether their bank's model risk team has weighed in on agentic finance platform selection.
3. **The Truist consumer loan sale signal**: Seven point seven billion dollars of consumer loans moving to Carlyle is a live example of balance sheet restructuring driven by the commercial-versus-consumer bifurcation. Ask peer CFOs whether their own portfolio mix, provisioning assumptions, and capital allocation plans reflect the same bifurcation -- or whether the Q4 plan still assumes a consumer recovery that is not materializing.
