I now have comprehensive fresh data across all required domains. Let me compile both outputs with what is genuinely new for November 13, 2026.
---
## Finance Pulse | Friday, November 13, 2026
**Bottom line: Today's October PPI release, arriving with a consensus forecast of six point six percent year-over-year and sitting squarely on the Fed's desk before December ninth, is the week's closing data punch; New York Fed President Williams speaks this evening as the first permanent FOMC voter to address markets after the hot CPI, and what he says about the fifty-basis-point door will define the weekend rate narrative -- meanwhile the super-regional cohort is absorbing a new and underappreciated balance-sheet shock as rising long-end yields drove a one point six billion dollar AOCI hit at Fifth Third alone, a harbinger of the Q4 mark-to-market pressure CFOs across the cohort are quietly modeling right now.**
---
### Top Takeaways
1. **Today's October PPI is the week's last inflation data point before the December ninth Fed decision.** Consensus expects headline producer prices at six point six percent year-over-year, up from six point three in September, following a September month-over-month that shocked at one point three percent. Even at consensus, this would be the highest annual PPI since November 2022, compressing any residual hope of a Fed pause.
2. **NY Fed President Williams speaks tonight -- and his remarks carry decisive weight.** Williams is a permanent FOMC voter and the Committee's vice chair. He speaks two days after the hot CPI, making this the first scheduled opportunity for a core policymaker to either ratify or push back on the fifty-basis-point scenario that Waller opened. CFOs need to listen.
3. **Fifth Third's post-Comerica integration is producing a new rate-sensitivity signal.** Rising long-end yields drove a one point six billion dollar reduction in Fifth Third's accumulated other comprehensive income in Q3, a direct consequence of combining a larger securities portfolio at a moment of yield volatility. This is a live and underappreciated integration risk that is not fully priced into super-regional comps.
4. **Roughly half of financial services firms cannot consistently demonstrate ROI on agentic AI**, according to a November five report from Paris. Only five percent have institutionalized agentic AI at enterprise scale. This is the most credible current data point on the gap between vendor marketing and actual bank finance deployments.
5. **Basel III Endgame: still not finalized.** As of September thirty, no final rule has appeared in the Federal Register. Finalization is targeted for Q4 2026, but the clock is tight, and finance teams at Category I through III banks should continue treating this as a proposal in flux.
---
### Key Themes
**Theme 1 (New): The PPI-to-PCE pipeline and what it means for bank CFO December assumptions.** October PPI data, releasing this morning, feeds directly into the PCE price index -- the Fed's preferred inflation gauge -- which arrives November twenty-fifth. That PCE read is the last major data point before the December ninth decision. If PPI comes in at or above consensus, the PCE pipeline becomes hotter, reinforcing the case for a faster move. CFOs who are still planning against a single twenty-five-basis-point December hike are running a scenario that the data is steadily dismantling.
**Theme 2 (Evolving): The long-end yield shock is now a balance-sheet event, not just a planning assumption.** The ten-year Treasury crossed five point one two percent this morning, up more than thirteen basis points in a single session on Thursday. For bank treasurers and controllers, this is not an abstract rate-path question. It is a live AOCI compression event with direct CET1 capital implications, as Fifth Third's Q3 experience demonstrates. The finance function owns the measurement, the disclosure, and the hedging strategy.
**Theme 3 (New): The Williams speech tonight resets the fifty-basis-point probability curve.** Markets have been trading the fifty-basis-point risk as a thirteen percent tail since Waller's comments. Williams, as vice chair and permanent voter, has not yet spoken post-CPI. His framing tonight -- whether he treats fifty as theoretical or plausible -- will either compress or widen that tail going into the weekend. Scenario planning for December must now explicitly model both lanes.
---
### Banking Finance-Function
**NIM and Deposit Dynamics:** The re-emerging rate-hike cycle is reintroducing an asymmetry CFOs thought they had escaped. Asset-sensitive banks with meaningful variable-rate loan portfolios stand to benefit: Atlantic Union's CFO quantified the relationship at approximately three basis points of NIM expansion per twenty-five-basis-point hike in a quarter. But the benefit is offset by deposit repricing lag and by mix shift pressure as customers continue moving into higher-yielding products. Super-regionals must now separately model the asset-sensitivity benefit against the AOCI and funding-cost drag.
**Capital and AOCI:** The long-end yield spike is creating a widening gap between book capital and tangible common equity as securities portfolios reprice lower. When longer-term rates rise, the bonds a bank holds lose value on paper, and higher rates reduced Fifth Third's accumulated other comprehensive income by one point six billion dollars in the third quarter. With the ten-year now above five percent and threatening to move further, Q4 marks will be worse for any bank carrying a sizable held-to-maturity or available-for-sale portfolio. CFOs need to stress-test their AOCI buffer against a fifty-basis-point December scenario today.
**Super-Regional Cohort Update:** Morningstar rates Fifth Third as on track to integrate Comerica, raising its fair value estimate to fifty-seven dollars from fifty-six. Fifth Third now operates approximately one thousand four hundred twenty-nine banking centers and two thousand five hundred forty-nine ATMs following its Comerica acquisition, and raised its quarterly dividend to forty-two cents from forty cents in September 2026. The integration is a live finance-function event: two general ledgers, two planning cycles, two sets of regulatory reporting obligations converging simultaneously against a rising-rate backdrop.
UBS Group cut its price target on PNC Financial Services Group from two hundred eighty-six dollars to two hundred seventy-eight dollars while maintaining a buy rating, in a report on November second. KeyCorp declared its Q4 2026 preferred dividends payable December fifteenth, confirming capital distribution stability even as the rate environment tightens.
---
### Regulatory Radar
**Basel III Endgame:** As of September thirty, 2026, no final rule has appeared in the Federal Register. Compliance and finance teams at covered banks should treat the endgame as a proposal whose scope, calibration, and dates can still change, and track it through the consultation and final-rule stages rather than planning against the 2023 text. Based on the agencies' own estimates, CET1 requirements would fall by roughly five point two percent for regional banks in Category III and IV, largely through elimination of certain deductions. Category III and IV banks can choose whether to adopt the external ratings-based approach or continue under a revised standardized approach, giving mid-sized regional banks more flexibility than the largest GSIBs. The practical implication for finance transformation: capital planning models must maintain dual-scenario capability until the final rule actually lands.
**Federal Reserve AI Governance (SR 26-2):** US Federal SR 26-2, effective April 2026, extends SR 11-7 model risk management requirements explicitly to AI and ML systems in banking, requiring model inventory and classification, independent validation, performance monitoring, documentation, and board-level governance for all material banking AI systems. This is the exam-ready obligation that converts every agentic finance deployment into a model risk management event. Any bank piloting AI in regulatory reporting, stress testing, or treasury has a governance gap to close before the next exam cycle.
---
### AI in Finance
**The ROI Reality Check:** Roughly half of financial services firms cannot consistently demonstrate a return on their agentic AI initiatives and lack clear frameworks for assessing whether those initiatives deliver sufficient value to justify continued investment. Only about five percent of financial institutions surveyed have institutionalized the capabilities required to operate agentic AI at enterprise scale. For finance transformation consultants, this is the single most important data point in the room: the gap between vendor promise and enterprise reality remains enormous, and clients who have not yet built governance frameworks, model inventories, and clean data foundations are not close to that five percent.
**Where Real Deployments Are Happening:** In one documented deployment, a finance insight agent automated more than ninety percent of business intelligence work in nine months, compressing a transformation that had previously taken three years. As much as eighty percent of FP&A work is still spent extracting and packaging data and performing simple calculations, which is precisely why FP&A is the highest-ROI entry point. Organizations report thirty to fifty percent faster planning cycles and a structural shift from annual budgeting to continuous rolling forecasts within twelve months of deployment, with AP/AR automation delivering the fastest payback at thirty to sixty days.
**Vendor Moves:** OneStream recently announced the general availability of its Finance Agentic Layer, allowing CFO offices to deploy AI agents that interact directly with financial data models. This is a real product release, not a roadmap item, and positions OneStream directly against Oracle EPM and Workday Adaptive for the agentic FP&A budget at banks.
**CFO Agenda Connection:** CFOs deploying AI across three or more finance functions achieve close cycles seven days faster and reduce compliance costs forty to sixty percent, per Gartner 2026. For bank CFOs facing rising workloads in regulatory reporting and stress testing against flat or shrinking headcount, that compliance cost reduction is the investment thesis, not the FP&A efficiency story.
**Buying Pattern Signal:** Firms are converging on a hybrid sourcing model that balances building capabilities in-house for differentiation, buying packaged agentic solutions to accelerate deployment at scale, and working with partners for ecosystem depth. Banks are increasingly not choosing between build and buy -- they are doing both, which means the finance technology budget is bifurcating between platform spend (OneStream, Workday, Oracle, SAP) and point-solution spend on agentic workflow tools.
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
**The AOCI Disclosure Urgency:** With the ten-year at five point one two and PPI dropping this morning, controllers at every bank with a sizable securities portfolio face an immediate Q4 disclosure planning question. The finance function must quantify the impact, assess the hedging posture, and prepare board-level communication before year-end. This is a near-term workload spike that is not in most transformation roadmaps.
**Integration Finance at Fifth Third:** The Comerica integration is the live case study for finance transformation demand creation. Merging two planning cycles, two chart-of-accounts structures, and two regulatory reporting platforms against a rising-rate backdrop while managing a significant AOCI hit is exactly the kind of cost-versus-workload squeeze that drives outsized investment in EPM consolidation, close automation, and regulatory reporting platforms. The consultants in this space should be in those conversations now.
**November Twenty-Fifth PCE as the CFO's True Decision Point:** The October PCE, releasing November twenty-fifth, is the last major data input before December ninth. If today's PPI feeds through at or above consensus, the PCE pipeline gets hotter. CFOs who have not yet built the fifty-basis-point December scenario into their Q4 and 2027 planning models are behind the data.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The consensus framing treats the fifty-basis-point December scenario as a tail risk to be monitored. But look at it from the Fed's communication posture: Governor Waller explicitly said fifty should be "considered," Chicago Fed's Goolsbee called the inflation data "borderline disturbing," and Cleveland Fed's Hammack dissented in favor of moving faster at the last meeting. Williams speaks tonight. If he does not explicitly close the door on fifty, markets will move the probability from thirteen percent toward twenty or above over the weekend. Bank CFOs running scenario planning only against twenty-five basis points are not planning -- they are hoping.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **"Your Q4 AOCI stress test: have you sized the fifty-basis-point scenario?"** The ten-year is at five point one two and climbing. What does a further thirty-basis-point move do to your held-to-maturity and AFS portfolio, and does your capital ratio stay above your internal trigger?
2. **"The five percent problem in agentic AI: where does your bank land?"** Only one in twenty financial institutions has institutionalized agentic AI at enterprise scale. Before your next AI investment decision, can you demonstrate ROI on the pilots you already have running?

## Finance Pulse | Friday, November 13, 2026
**Bottom line: Today's October PPI release, arriving with a consensus forecast of six point six percent year-over-year and sitting squarely on the Fed's desk before December ninth, is the week's closing data punch; New York Fed President Williams speaks this evening as the first permanent FOMC voter to address markets after the hot CPI, and what he says about the fifty-basis-point door will define the weekend rate narrative -- meanwhile the super-regional cohort is absorbing a new and underappreciated balance-sheet shock as rising long-end yields drove a one point six billion dollar AOCI hit at Fifth Third alone, a harbinger of the Q4 mark-to-market pressure CFOs across the cohort are quietly modeling right now.**
---
### Top Takeaways
1. **Today's October PPI is the week's last inflation data point before the December ninth Fed decision.** Consensus expects headline producer prices at six point six percent year-over-year, up from six point three in September, following a September month-over-month that shocked at one point three percent. Even at consensus, this would be the highest annual PPI since November 2022, compressing any residual hope of a Fed pause.
2. **NY Fed President Williams speaks tonight -- and his remarks carry decisive weight.** Williams is a permanent FOMC voter and the Committee's vice chair. He speaks two days after the hot CPI, making this the first scheduled opportunity for a core policymaker to either ratify or push back on the fifty-basis-point scenario that Waller opened. CFOs need to listen.
3. **Fifth Third's post-Comerica integration is producing a new rate-sensitivity signal.** Rising long-end yields drove a one point six billion dollar reduction in Fifth Third's accumulated other comprehensive income in Q3, a direct consequence of combining a larger securities portfolio at a moment of yield volatility. This is a live and underappreciated integration risk that is not fully priced into super-regional comps.
4. **Roughly half of financial services firms cannot consistently demonstrate ROI on agentic AI**, according to a November five report from Paris. Only five percent have institutionalized agentic AI at enterprise scale. This is the most credible current data point on the gap between vendor marketing and actual bank finance deployments.
5. **Basel III Endgame: still not finalized.** As of September thirty, no final rule has appeared in the Federal Register. Finalization is targeted for Q4 2026, but the clock is tight, and finance teams at Category I through III banks should continue treating this as a proposal in flux.
---
### Key Themes
**Theme 1 (New): The PPI-to-PCE pipeline and what it means for bank CFO December assumptions.** October PPI data, releasing this morning, feeds directly into the PCE price index -- the Fed's preferred inflation gauge -- which arrives November twenty-fifth. That PCE read is the last major data point before the December ninth decision. If PPI comes in at or above consensus, the PCE pipeline becomes hotter, reinforcing the case for a faster move. CFOs who are still planning against a single twenty-five-basis-point December hike are running a scenario that the data is steadily dismantling.
**Theme 2 (Evolving): The long-end yield shock is now a balance-sheet event, not just a planning assumption.** The ten-year Treasury crossed five point one two percent this morning, up more than thirteen basis points in a single session on Thursday. For bank treasurers and controllers, this is not an abstract rate-path question. It is a live AOCI compression event with direct CET1 capital implications, as Fifth Third's Q3 experience demonstrates. The finance function owns the measurement, the disclosure, and the hedging strategy.
**Theme 3 (New): The Williams speech tonight resets the fifty-basis-point probability curve.** Markets have been trading the fifty-basis-point risk as a thirteen percent tail since Waller's comments. Williams, as vice chair and permanent voter, has not yet spoken post-CPI. His framing tonight -- whether he treats fifty as theoretical or plausible -- will either compress or widen that tail going into the weekend. Scenario planning for December must now explicitly model both lanes.
---
### Banking Finance-Function
**NIM and Deposit Dynamics:** The re-emerging rate-hike cycle is reintroducing an asymmetry CFOs thought they had escaped. Asset-sensitive banks with meaningful variable-rate loan portfolios stand to benefit: Atlantic Union's CFO quantified the relationship at approximately three basis points of NIM expansion per twenty-five-basis-point hike in a quarter. But the benefit is offset by deposit repricing lag and by mix shift pressure as customers continue moving into higher-yielding products. Super-regionals must now separately model the asset-sensitivity benefit against the AOCI and funding-cost drag.
**Capital and AOCI:** The long-end yield spike is creating a widening gap between book capital and tangible common equity as securities portfolios reprice lower. When longer-term rates rise, the bonds a bank holds lose value on paper, and higher rates reduced Fifth Third's accumulated other comprehensive income by one point six billion dollars in the third quarter. With the ten-year now above five percent and threatening to move further, Q4 marks will be worse for any bank carrying a sizable held-to-maturity or available-for-sale portfolio. CFOs need to stress-test their AOCI buffer against a fifty-basis-point December scenario today.
**Super-Regional Cohort Update:** Morningstar rates Fifth Third as on track to integrate Comerica, raising its fair value estimate to fifty-seven dollars from fifty-six. Fifth Third now operates approximately one thousand four hundred twenty-nine banking centers and two thousand five hundred forty-nine ATMs following its Comerica acquisition, and raised its quarterly dividend to forty-two cents from forty cents in September 2026. The integration is a live finance-function event: two general ledgers, two planning cycles, two sets of regulatory reporting obligations converging simultaneously against a rising-rate backdrop.
UBS Group cut its price target on PNC Financial Services Group from two hundred eighty-six dollars to two hundred seventy-eight dollars while maintaining a buy rating, in a report on November second. KeyCorp declared its Q4 2026 preferred dividends payable December fifteenth, confirming capital distribution stability even as the rate environment tightens.
---
### Regulatory Radar
**Basel III Endgame:** As of September thirty, 2026, no final rule has appeared in the Federal Register. Compliance and finance teams at covered banks should treat the endgame as a proposal whose scope, calibration, and dates can still change, and track it through the consultation and final-rule stages rather than planning against the 2023 text. Based on the agencies' own estimates, CET1 requirements would fall by roughly five point two percent for regional banks in Category III and IV, largely through elimination of certain deductions. Category III and IV banks can choose whether to adopt the external ratings-based approach or continue under a revised standardized approach, giving mid-sized regional banks more flexibility than the largest GSIBs. The practical implication for finance transformation: capital planning models must maintain dual-scenario capability until the final rule actually lands.
**Federal Reserve AI Governance (SR 26-2):** US Federal SR 26-2, effective April 2026, extends SR 11-7 model risk management requirements explicitly to AI and ML systems in banking, requiring model inventory and classification, independent validation, performance monitoring, documentation, and board-level governance for all material banking AI systems. This is the exam-ready obligation that converts every agentic finance deployment into a model risk management event. Any bank piloting AI in regulatory reporting, stress testing, or treasury has a governance gap to close before the next exam cycle.
---
### AI in Finance
**The ROI Reality Check:** Roughly half of financial services firms cannot consistently demonstrate a return on their agentic AI initiatives and lack clear frameworks for assessing whether those initiatives deliver sufficient value to justify continued investment. Only about five percent of financial institutions surveyed have institutionalized the capabilities required to operate agentic AI at enterprise scale. For finance transformation consultants, this is the single most important data point in the room: the gap between vendor promise and enterprise reality remains enormous, and clients who have not yet built governance frameworks, model inventories, and clean data foundations are not close to that five percent.
**Where Real Deployments Are Happening:** In one documented deployment, a finance insight agent automated more than ninety percent of business intelligence work in nine months, compressing a transformation that had previously taken three years. As much as eighty percent of FP&A work is still spent extracting and packaging data and performing simple calculations, which is precisely why FP&A is the highest-ROI entry point. Organizations report thirty to fifty percent faster planning cycles and a structural shift from annual budgeting to continuous rolling forecasts within twelve months of deployment, with AP/AR automation delivering the fastest payback at thirty to sixty days.
**Vendor Moves:** OneStream recently announced the general availability of its Finance Agentic Layer, allowing CFO offices to deploy AI agents that interact directly with financial data models. This is a real product release, not a roadmap item, and positions OneStream directly against Oracle EPM and Workday Adaptive for the agentic FP&A budget at banks.
**CFO Agenda Connection:** CFOs deploying AI across three or more finance functions achieve close cycles seven days faster and reduce compliance costs forty to sixty percent, per Gartner 2026. For bank CFOs facing rising workloads in regulatory reporting and stress testing against flat or shrinking headcount, that compliance cost reduction is the investment thesis, not the FP&A efficiency story.
**Buying Pattern Signal:** Firms are converging on a hybrid sourcing model that balances building capabilities in-house for differentiation, buying packaged agentic solutions to accelerate deployment at scale, and working with partners for ecosystem depth. Banks are increasingly not choosing between build and buy -- they are doing both, which means the finance technology budget is bifurcating between platform spend (OneStream, Workday, Oracle, SAP) and point-solution spend on agentic workflow tools.
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
**The AOCI Disclosure Urgency:** With the ten-year at five point one two and PPI dropping this morning, controllers at every bank with a sizable securities portfolio face an immediate Q4 disclosure planning question. The finance function must quantify the impact, assess the hedging posture, and prepare board-level communication before year-end. This is a near-term workload spike that is not in most transformation roadmaps.
**Integration Finance at Fifth Third:** The Comerica integration is the live case study for finance transformation demand creation. Merging two planning cycles, two chart-of-accounts structures, and two regulatory reporting platforms against a rising-rate backdrop while managing a significant AOCI hit is exactly the kind of cost-versus-workload squeeze that drives outsized investment in EPM consolidation, close automation, and regulatory reporting platforms. The consultants in this space should be in those conversations now.
**November Twenty-Fifth PCE as the CFO's True Decision Point:** The October PCE, releasing November twenty-fifth, is the last major data input before December ninth. If today's PPI feeds through at or above consensus, the PCE pipeline gets hotter. CFOs who have not yet built the fifty-basis-point December scenario into their Q4 and 2027 planning models are behind the data.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The consensus framing treats the fifty-basis-point December scenario as a tail risk to be monitored. But look at it from the Fed's communication posture: Governor Waller explicitly said fifty should be "considered," Chicago Fed's Goolsbee called the inflation data "borderline disturbing," and Cleveland Fed's Hammack dissented in favor of moving faster at the last meeting. Williams speaks tonight. If he does not explicitly close the door on fifty, markets will move the probability from thirteen percent toward twenty or above over the weekend. Bank CFOs running scenario planning only against twenty-five basis points are not planning -- they are hoping.
---

3. **"The Basel Endgame is still a proposal -- but it is redesigning your capital planning model today."** Category III and IV banks have optionality on the ratings-based approach that the largest GSIBs do not. Are you modeling both paths, or are you waiting for finalization to run the analysis?

item.title: Finance Pulse - Nov 12, 2026
item.description:
I'll run all major searches simultaneously across macro, rates, banking, regulatory, and AI-in-finance domains to capture the freshest developments as of November 12, 2026.I now have strong, sourced material across all required domains. Let me compile both outputs with what is genuinely new for November 12, 2026, avoiding all recycled themes from prior episodes.
---
## Finance Pulse | Thursday, November 12, 2026
**Bottom line: The Cleveland Fed's live November nowcast lands today with PCE tracking at three point nine four percent year-over-year and CPI core heading toward three point three two percent, making a December hike near-certain but forcing CFOs to price a new and underappreciated scenario: a March 2027 follow-on hike that pushes peak funding costs to four point five percent, while the super-regional cohort is simultaneously repricing two distinct risks -- Truist's unfavorable deposit mix is already squeezing NIM guidance, and KeyCorp's four billion dollar unrealized bond loss creates a capital overhang that distorts its regulatory CET1 by over two hundred basis points relative to its reported ratio.**
---
### Top Takeaways
1. The Cleveland Fed's November nowcast, updated through November 10, shows CPI at three point eight three percent and core PCE at three point three two percent year-over-year -- the first live November inflation read of this tightening cycle, confirming that the post-October CPI acceleration is not reverting. 2. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan has explicitly called for two additional quarter-point hikes, adding an institutional voice to what Goldman Sachs's forecast revision established. This is now a multi-voice consensus, not a single-bank outlier. 3. U.S. Bancorp's acquisition of capital markets firm BTIG closed June 1, 2026 -- a fee-income diversification move that is newly relevant as super-regionals face peak funding cost pressure and need noninterest revenue to offset NIM compression. 4. KeyCorp's unrealized bond losses of three point eight six five billion dollars create an AOCI-adjusted CET1 of nine percent against a reported eleven point one percent -- the exact type of AOCI gap that the Basel III re-proposal's Category III and IV AOCI recognition requirement (a three point one percent add, five-year phase-in) will begin to close, raising finance-function modeling complexity for mid-tier banks. 5. PwC's 2026 Digital Trends survey finds eighty-three percent of respondents believe AI agents will break down functional silos in finance -- yet only twenty-seven percent have fully embedded an AI strategy, the most credible current measure of the gap between aspiration and deployment.
---
### Key Themes
**Theme 1 (New): November inflation nowcast as a live CFO planning signal** The Cleveland Fed's daily nowcast now shows November PCE running at three point nine four percent year-over-year and core PCE at three point three two percent as of November 10. This is the first time finance teams have a live, daily November read before the official release. For bank CFOs, this tool changes the cadence of scenario refresh: deposit cost assumptions, NII sensitivity tables, and ALCO presentations can be updated continuously rather than waiting for month-end data drops.
**Theme 2 (Evolving): The deposit mix problem is shifting from an industry-level theme to a bank-specific differentiator** Truist has already cut its net interest income growth outlook to one to one and a half percent, citing an unfavorable deposit mix. This is a materially different position from peers like U.S. Bancorp, where average deposits grew two point nine percent year-over-year, or KeyCorp, where client deposits rose one point six percent. The divergence in mix -- not just rate sensitivity -- is now the primary differentiator of NIM trajectory heading into a potential two-hike sequence.
**Theme 3 (New): The Anaplan Agentic Enterprise delay signals the gap between platform marketing and production readiness** Anaplan announced its Agentic Enterprise suite -- skills-based agents for the CFO's office covering FP&A, treasury, controllership, and procurement, deployed on Amazon Bedrock -- for October 2026 general availability. As of November 2026, it had not confirmed GA. This is the most concrete evidence available that the agentic finance platform market is ahead of its delivery schedule, and a direct signal to bank buyers evaluating vendor roadmaps.
---
### Banking Finance-Function
Third-quarter results from PNC, U.S. Bancorp, Truist, Fifth Third, Regions, and KeyCorp show regional banks embedding AI into everyday operations, while U.S. Bancorp reported average total loans up eight percent year-over-year with average commercial loans reaching one hundred fifty-five point four billion dollars, up twelve point three percent from a year earlier.
Truist has cut its net interest income growth outlook to one to one and a half percent, explicitly citing an unfavorable deposit mix as the driver. Truist bought back one point one billion dollars of stock in Q1 and one point two billion in Q2, with CET1 capital rising to ten point nine percent; management has indicated it wants that ratio at ten percent by end of 2027, implying continued capital return.
KeyCorp carries three point eight six five billion dollars in unrealized bond losses. Including those losses, its CET1 ratio is nine percent, compared with eleven point one percent on the regulatory basis -- a two-hundred-plus basis point gap that AOCI accounting changes in the Basel re-proposal will progressively narrow.
U.S. Bancorp added capital markets firm BTIG on June 1, 2026, and is the only bank in the super-regional peer group to raise its dividend this year, lifting the quarterly payout from fifty-two to fifty-four cents.
---
### Regulatory Radar
The Basel III Endgame re-proposal, issued March 19, 2026, saw its comment period close June 18, 2026, with no final rule issued as of mid-October. The rulebook currently exists in two states: the 2013 rule remains binding law, and the March 2026 proposals are pending finalization.
Fed staff estimate cumulative CET1 changes of negative four point eight percent for Categories I and II, negative five point two percent for Categories III and IV, and negative seven point eight percent below the one hundred billion dollar threshold, against a positive sixteen percent impact from the 2023 package. AOCI recognition for Categories III and IV adds a positive three point one percent over a five-year phase-in -- the specific provision that creates new accounting complexity for super-regional banks like KeyCorp.
KPMG notes that the net capital relief from the re-proposal could create opportunities for banks to reassess binding constraints, release excess management buffers, and redeploy capital toward lending growth, balance sheet optimization, and M&A.
---
### AI in Finance
**Adoption reality check:** Forty-four percent of finance teams now use agentic AI in FP&A in 2026, a six-hundred-percent-plus year-over-year increase per Wolters Kluwer, and fully deployed teams report a one point eight day close versus a six point two day average per the Hackett Group.
**The aspiration-to-deployment gap:** PwC's 2026 Digital Trends in Operations Survey found that eighty-three percent of respondents believe AI agents and automation will accelerate the breakdown of traditional functional silos, yet only twenty-seven percent have fully embedded an AI strategy. This gap is wider in banking than in other industries, given data fragmentation across core systems, regulatory constraints on model governance, and the absence of clean ERP data layers in most super-regionals.
**Vendor movement:** Anaplan announced its Agentic Enterprise -- skills-based agents for the CFO's office covering FP&A, treasury, controllership, and procurement, deployed on Amazon Bedrock -- for October 2026. As of November 2026, it had not confirmed general availability. Anthropic's Claude Cowork, the agentic workspace launched in January 2026, is being used by FP&A and controllership teams for forecasting, variance, close, and consolidation.
**CFO agenda connection:** BCG finds that as much as eighty percent of FP&A work is still spent extracting and packaging data and performing simple calculations; agentic AI will move finance teams from producing reports to interpreting performance and advising the business. In one documented deployment, a finance insight agent automated more than ninety percent of business intelligence work in nine months -- work that previously took three years. For bank CFOs facing rising workloads against flat or falling headcount budgets, this is the core ROI case.
**Governance signal:** Global watchdogs have called for tighter controls on agentic AI in finance, citing concerns over autonomous decision-making that could lead to systemic errors or compliance breaches. AI governance for financial outputs is emerging as a board-level priority, driven by EY's September 2026 AI Risk and Governance Survey findings on the confidence gap.
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
U.S. Bank's own November 2026 economic outlook forecasts two additional twenty-five-basis-point Fed rate increases by early 2027, bringing the federal funds rate to four point two five to four point five percent, with risks increasingly tilted toward a longer tightening cycle -- framing the challenge not as whether inflation warrants continued restraint, but how much additional tightening is appropriate when borrowing costs are already elevated.
Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan, speaking after the October CPI report, said she sees a need for two additional quarter-point increases and expressed concern that PCE could also move higher when reported later in November.
The Cleveland Fed's live nowcast as of November 10 shows November PCE at three point nine four percent year-over-year and core CPI at three point three two percent -- real-time confirmation that November is tracking hotter than October.
For finance transformation consultants, the demand signal is now explicit: banks facing a potential four point five percent peak rate, AOCI recognition changes in the Basel re-proposal, Anaplan delivery slippage, and an eighty-three-to-twenty-seven percent aspiration-to-deployment gap in AI strategy need a coherent sequencing of platform modernization, model governance, and scenario infrastructure -- not point solutions purchased one workflow at a time.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The conventional narrative is that higher-for-longer rates are universally bad for bank NIMs due to deposit repricing pressure. The contrarian read: banks with the discipline to shift wholesale and brokered funding to core deposits at the right moment in the cycle can expand NIM even as rates rise. The evidence is in the Q4 earnings data from smaller banks reporting this week -- Camden National expanded NIM fifteen basis points by cutting higher-cost borrowings by twenty-six percent through core deposit growth, and QCR Holdings reduced wholesale and brokered funding through the same playbook. The CFO transformation implication is that liability management analytics and deposit modeling capability -- not just asset repricing -- is now the differentiating infrastructure investment.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **The nowcast CFO planning model:** The Cleveland Fed's daily November nowcast gives bank finance teams their first real-time November inflation signal before month-end data. Ask your client: is their ALCO scenario refresh cadence built for daily data, or is it still running on a monthly CPI-release calendar? That gap is a process transformation opportunity.
2. **The AOCI cliff for mid-tier banks:** KeyCorp's two-hundred-plus basis point gap between regulatory and AOCI-adjusted CET1 is not unique. Any Category III or IV bank with significant unrealized securities losses faces the five-year phase-in of AOCI recognition under the Basel re-proposal. Ask: has the finance function modeled the capital trajectory and stress scenarios under each AOCI phase-in scenario?
3. **Anaplan's GA slip as a vendor-selection lesson:** The Agentic Enterprise suite missed its October GA date. For banks in platform evaluation, this is the moment to ask vendors: what is the contractual commitment to production availability, and what does the reference customer list for agentic finance deployments actually look like in banking specifically?

The Cleveland Fed's live nowcast as of November 10 shows November PCE at three point nine four percent year-over-year and core CPI at three point three two percent -- real-time confirmation that November is tracking hotter than October.
For finance transformation consultants, the demand signal is now explicit: banks facing a potential four point five percent peak rate, AOCI recognition changes in the Basel re-proposal, Anaplan delivery slippage, and an eighty-three-to-twenty-seven percent aspiration-to-deployment gap in AI strategy need a coherent sequencing of platform modernization, model governance, and scenario infrastructure -- not point solutions purchased one workflow at a time.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The conventional narrative is that higher-for-longer rates are universally bad for bank NIMs due to deposit repricing pressure. The contrarian read: banks with the discipline to shift wholesale and brokered funding to core deposits at the right moment in the cycle can expand NIM even as rates rise. The evidence is in the Q4 earnings data from smaller banks reporting this week -- Camden National expanded NIM fifteen basis points by cutting higher-cost borrowings by twenty-six percent through core deposit growth, and QCR Holdings reduced wholesale and brokered funding through the same playbook. The CFO transformation implication is that liability management analytics and deposit modeling capability -- not just asset repricing -- is now the differentiating infrastructure investment.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **The nowcast CFO planning model:** The Cleveland Fed's daily November nowcast gives bank finance teams their first real-time November inflation signal before month-end data. Ask your client: is their ALCO scenario refresh cadence built for daily data, or is it still running on a monthly CPI-release calendar? That gap is a process transformation opportunity.
2. **The AOCI cliff for mid-tier banks:** KeyCorp's two-hundred-plus basis point gap between regulatory and AOCI-adjusted CET1 is not unique. Any Category III or IV bank with significant unrealized securities losses faces the five-year phase-in of AOCI recognition under the Basel re-proposal. Ask: has the finance function modeled the capital trajectory and stress scenarios under each AOCI phase-in scenario?
3. **Anaplan's GA slip as a vendor-selection lesson:** The Agentic Enterprise suite missed its October GA date. For banks in platform evaluation, this is the moment to ask vendors: what is the contractual commitment to production availability, and what does the reference customer list for agentic finance deployments actually look like in banking specifically?

item.title: Finance Pulse - Nov 11, 2026
item.description:
I now have comprehensive, fresh data across all required domains. Here are the genuinely new angles for November 11, 2026, not covered in prior episodes:
1. **Goldman Sachs has just added a March 2027 hike to its forecast**, making it the first major bank to revise post-CPI. The rate-path implication for bank CFOs is now a peak of four point two five to four point five percent, with first cut deferred to December 2027. This is a materially different planning horizon than yesterday's briefing.
2. **The 50-basis-point December debate is entirely new territory**: Governor Waller opened the door to a supersized hike, with market odds briefly touching fifteen percent before settling near eleven percent. This is a new asymmetric risk for bank CFO scenario planning.
3. **McKinsey's Global Banking Annual Review (published November 10) drops a landmark warning**: AI agent token costs at banks could reach twenty percent of total labor costs, prompting a new institutional response -- dedicated "AI FinOps" teams. This is a completely new angle on AI ROI at banks.
4. **Dallas Fed survey (October 27 to November 4)**: Eleven point four percent of banks have already restricted customer AI agent access to online banking. The funding cost secondary effect of customer-facing AI is a new and underexplored angle.
5. **Basel III Endgame**: No final rule as of September 30, 2026 -- finalization in Q4 2026 still the target, but this is unchanged. One line and move on.
6. **KBRA data point**: Average bank NIM hit three point nine four percent in Q2 2026, up forty-three basis points from the Q3 2024 trough -- but the September hike and now December's near-certain move threaten to re-widen deposit cost spreads. This reversal story is fresh.
---
## Finance Pulse | Wednesday, November 11, 2026
**Bottom line: Goldman Sachs became the first major bank to add a March 2027 hike to its Fed forecast this morning, extending the peak funds rate to as high as four point two five to four point five percent and deferring first rate cuts to December 2027 -- a planning-horizon shift that invalidates most bank CFO NIM and deposit-cost models built in Q3; simultaneously, McKinsey's new Global Banking Annual Review warns that AI agent token spending at banks could reach twenty percent of total labor costs, triggering a new institutional discipline called "AI FinOps" that is fast becoming the most consequential finance-function operating model question of the cycle.**
---
### Top Takeaways
1. Goldman Sachs has added a March 2027 rate hike to its forecast after the third consecutive month of above-consensus inflation, pushing its projected peak funds rate to four point two five to four point five percent and deferring the first cut to December 2027 -- the most hawkish major-bank call now on the table. 2. The December meeting is no longer just a twenty-five-basis-point certainty: Governor Waller explicitly said fifty basis points "should be considered" if inflation stays hot, briefly pushing supersized hike odds to fifteen percent and permanently changing the CFO scenario-planning distribution. 3. McKinsey's Global Banking Annual Review (published November 10) finds that AI agent token costs at banks could reach twenty percent of total labor costs, with banks now forming dedicated "AI FinOps" teams to manage spending -- a structural shift in how finance transformation investments are governed and budgeted. 4. KBRA data shows average bank NIM recovered to three point nine four percent in Q2 2026 from its three point five one percent trough -- but the resuming hike cycle threatens to re-accelerate deposit repricing and erode those gains through 2027. 5. A Dallas Fed survey of seventy bankers finds eleven point four percent of institutions have already restricted customer AI agent access to online banking systems -- and McKinsey warns those same customer AI agents are already being used to hunt for higher-yield savings accounts, creating a new and AI-driven deposit migration risk.
---
### Key Themes
**Theme 1 (New): The 50bps December Debate Changes CFO Scenario Architecture** Until yesterday, bank CFOs were stress-testing one scenario: a twenty-five-basis-point December hike followed by a possible pause. The opening of a fifty-basis-point debate by a voting Fed governor introduces a genuinely asymmetric risk. For a CFO building the 2027 budget, the difference between a four percent and four point five percent terminal rate is not marginal -- it reshapes deposit beta assumptions, funding mix optimization, and the entire NIM trajectory.
**Theme 2 (New): AI Agent Costs as a Finance P&L Line** McKinsey's finding that token costs could hit twenty percent of labor spend reframes AI in finance from a capability question to a cost-structure question. For bank CFOs who have been authorizing pilot expansions on the assumption that agentic AI is fundamentally deflationary, this is a corrective signal. The emergence of "AI FinOps" as an institutional function -- with dedicated teams managing token budgets -- signals that AI spend is now competing directly with headcount in the finance cost base.
**Theme 3 (Evolving): NIM Recovery Under Renewed Threat** KBRA documents a forty-three-basis-point NIM recovery from Q3 2024 to Q2 2026, driven primarily by declining deposit costs rather than rising asset yields. That improvement is now at risk. The September hike already re-introduced funding pressure; Goldman's March 2027 call means deposit repricing could run for another eighteen months.
---
### Banking Finance-Function Metrics
Average cost of total funding fell thirty-six basis points to one point eight seven percent in Q2 2026, and average cost of total deposits dropped thirty-one basis points to one point eight one percent over the same period from their Q3 2024 peaks. Average NIM increased to three point nine four percent in Q2 2026 from three point five one percent in Q3 2024, a forty-three-basis-point improvement, while earning-asset yields increased only modestly over the same period. Those funding cost gains are now squarely in the crosshairs of the renewed tightening cycle.
Despite the relief banks enjoyed through easing deposit costs, the Fed's September hike and consequent October hold stand to reintroduce funding pressures and competition in the marketplace. With Goldman now forecasting a March 2027 follow-on, the deposit repricing clock resets again.
---
### Regulatory Radar
**Basel III Endgame:** No change since the June 18 comment-period close. As of September 30, 2026, no final rule appeared in the Federal Register. Compliance and finance teams at covered banks should treat the endgame as a proposal whose scope, calibration, and dates can still change. Implementation is diverging globally: the UK's PRA finalized its "Basel 3.1" package for January 2027 and the EU is phasing in temporary mitigations through 2029. The divergence itself is a CFO risk: banks with cross-border books face a patchwork of go-live dates rather than a synchronized international standard.
---
### AI in Finance
**The McKinsey Cost Warning (the day's dominant signal):** Banks worldwide are trying to curb the soaring cost of AI agents, as spending on the tokens that power them could easily reach twenty percent of total labor costs, according to McKinsey's Global Banking Annual Review. When AI agents are working and communicating with each other, tokens quickly add up, breaking traditional cost-management approaches.
Some banks have already created "AI FinOps" teams to control spending, while increasingly focusing deployments on areas with the strongest expected returns. This is the clearest signal yet that AI in banking has moved from pilot enthusiasm to a disciplined ROI conversation.
**The human oversight cost revelation:** When an agent performs a customer service task in banking, token costs account for only twenty to twenty-five percent of variable run costs, while human oversight accounts for seventy to seventy-five percent, with sixty percent of an agentic task's cost tied to refining answers rather than producing the first answer. This overturns the assumption that agentic AI primarily saves headcount -- supervision cost is currently the dominant cost driver.
**Customer-facing AI as a deposit threat:** A McKinsey survey of forty-six thousand retail banking customers worldwide found that most already use AI to compare banking services, locate higher-yield savings accounts, and refinance or consolidate debt. Among those AI users, seventy-two percent said they would let a banking agent complete one financial task, though they would limit autonomous approvals to five hundred dollars. McKinsey notes that while AI agents may help banks raise revenue and reduce costs, they could also weigh on profits by moving deposits out of non-interest-bearing accounts and into higher-yielding ones.
**Banks' institutional response:** In a recently released survey of seventy bankers, the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas found that eleven point four percent said their institution or service provider had taken steps to restrict existing or prospective customers' AI agent activity on online banking platforms. More than a quarter of respondents said they did not know whether their institution had restricted AI agent activity, while thirty-eight point six percent said no restrictions had been implemented and were not planned.
**CFO Agenda connection:** The convergence of token cost escalation and AI-driven deposit migration creates a double-sided CFO problem. On the cost side, uncontrolled agentic deployments in finance (FP&A, close, treasury) are eroding the efficiency savings they were meant to generate. On the revenue side, customer-facing AI is accelerating the deposit repricing that the September hike had already re-ignited. Banks need to manage both simultaneously.
**OneStream Finance Agentic Layer:** OneStream recently announced the general availability of its Finance Agentic Layer, allowing CFO offices to deploy AI agents that interact directly with financial data models. This is a named, production-stage vendor move -- not a roadmap promise -- and directly relevant to bank finance-platform buying decisions.
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
The Goldman March 2027 call is a planning event, not just a market data point. Goldman Sachs now sees twenty-five-basis-point Fed hikes in both December 2026 and March 2027, adding a third hike to the cycle after a third straight month of hot inflation, and David Mericle said the recent readings will lead most FOMC participants to signal a third hike in the December dot plot. Goldman now expects rate cuts to begin in December 2027, three months later than previously forecast, followed by additional cuts in March, June, and September 2028. Any bank CFO whose 2027 operating plan assumed a mid-year cut needs to rebuild that model today.
Deloitte's Q4 2025 CFO Signals survey found that fifty-four percent of CFOs say integrating AI agents into their finance departments will be a top transformation priority in 2026, and eighty-seven percent believe AI will be extremely or very important to finance operations. But the McKinsey cost data now puts a price tag on that priority -- and it is not cheap.
A Gartner report found that close to sixty percent of finance teams are piloting or implementing AI projects, while only seven percent of CFOs say those investments are having a strong impact. The gap between pilot breadth and demonstrated impact is the central governance challenge for bank finance transformation leaders heading into 2027 budget season.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The McKinsey report is being read as a cost-escalation warning. But the more strategically important finding is the deposit migration signal buried in the same report. Customer AI agents are already hunting for yield on behalf of depositors. Banks that restrict access to external AI agents -- the eleven percent doing so today -- are protecting their non-interest-bearing deposit base in the short term. But that is a defensive posture, not a strategy. The banks that build their own customer-facing AI agents, with controlled access and embedded product cross-sell, will shape where deposits flow rather than simply trying to dam them. For a CFO, this reframes AI platform investment from a cost-reduction project to a funding-economics defense.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **"Your 2027 NIM model assumes cuts starting when?"** Goldman now has the first cut in December 2027. If your client's plan has mid-2027 relief baked in, that model needs a rebuild -- and the deposit beta trajectory through eighteen more months of elevated rates is the core assumption to pressure-test.
2. **"Have you sized your AI agent token budget?"** McKinsey says token costs could reach twenty percent of labor spend, and some banks are already building dedicated AI FinOps teams. Ask your client whether their finance transformation business case includes a token-cost assumption -- and whether the human oversight cost (seventy to seventy-five percent of agentic task costs) is in the model.
3. **"What is your strategy if customer AI agents start routing your depositors to competitors?"** McKinsey's survey of forty-six thousand customers shows most already use AI to find higher-yield accounts. The banks blocking external agent access are buying time, not solving the problem. What is your client's answer?

item.title: Finance Pulse - Nov 10, 2026
item.description:
I now have strong sourced material across all required domains. Let me compile both outputs, making sure everything genuinely new for November 10 is foregrounded, with no recycled themes from prior episodes.
---
## Finance Pulse | Tuesday, November 10, 2026
**Bottom line: The October CPI print lands this morning as the final inflation data point before the December ninth Fed decision, and with no year-over-year comparison available, the month-over-month read is the only honest signal the market has; December hike odds have climbed to eighty-four percent on CME FedWatch, the highest of this tightening cycle, introducing a new and underappreciated scenario where the Fed hikes twice more into 2027 rather than stopping in December -- a possibility that rewrites bank CFO planning assumptions on funding costs, deposit beta, and NIM trajectory for the full year ahead.**
---
### Top Takeaways
1. CME FedWatch printed an eighty-four point four percent December hike probability this morning, up from seventy-seven percent just four days ago, with UBS now projecting a second hike in March 2027. The "one and done" framing that dominated last week's planning conversations is now a minority view.
2. The October CPI is released today at eight-thirty Eastern. Street consensus is zero point three percent month-over-month headline and zero point two percent core. A hot print above zero point three percent effectively seals December; a print of zero point one percent core or below, per Bank of America's analysis, is the only scenario that meaningfully shifts expectations toward a pause.
3. Capgemini data published November fifth shows roughly half of financial services firms cannot consistently demonstrate ROI on their agentic AI initiatives and only five percent have achieved enterprise-wide orchestration -- the first credible quantitative reality check on agentic AI hype that finance transformation buyers at banks should be anchoring.
4. The Basel III Endgame re-proposal, with its comment period closed on June eighteenth, remains pending a final rule, but its structure has materially shifted: Category I and II banks face a projected one point six percent capital increase, far below the nine percent increase contemplated in the 2023 original.
5. A new DataTrek analysis argues that Wall Street's equity volatility is doing some of the Fed's tightening work for it, reducing the probability of additional hikes beyond December -- a nuanced point that matters for bank treasury teams modeling asset sensitivity and deposit repricing timelines.
---
### Key Themes
**Theme 1 (New): The "one and done" December hike assumption is breaking down.** Markets now price an eighty-four percent probability of a December hike and a meaningful probability of a March 2027 follow-through. This is a qualitatively new rate-path framing not present in any prior episode and is the dominant CFO planning variable today.
**Theme 2 (Evolving): Agentic AI hits the ROI wall.** The Capgemini report is the first sector-specific, quantified reality check on agentic finance deployments: half of firms cannot demonstrate return and only five percent have scaled to enterprise level. This shifts the client conversation from "are you piloting?" to "can you prove value?"
**Theme 3 (New): AI infrastructure spending as an inflation input.** Richmond Fed President Barkin flagged on November ninth that the massive wave of AI infrastructure spending is actively adding to near-term inflation by driving robust demand -- a linkage between the technology transformation agenda and the macro rate environment that has not appeared in any prior episode.
---
### Banking Finance-Function
The October jobs print of one hundred sixty-five thousand, against a consensus of sixty-five thousand, combined with today's CPI release, is now the dominant input to Q4 bank NIM planning. Banks that guided to static or modest NIM expansion assuming no December hike will need to revisit those assumptions. BankUnited's management guided Q4 2026 NIM to approximately three point two percent and net interest income to two hundred sixty-five million, explicitly assuming a December rate hike. That guidance now looks like the base case across asset-sensitive banks in the super-regional cohort.
Management noted the expected Q4 margin expansion is primarily tied to asset sensitivity, with loan yields expected to reprice faster than deposit costs, though BankUnited aims to keep its static balance sheet close to rate-neutral rather than make a directional rate bet. That posture -- asset-sensitive but not aggressively positioned -- captures where most super-regionals currently sit.
The new wrinkle for CFOs is the March 2027 hike scenario. UBS Wealth Management projected a continued, measured tightening cycle, starting with a twenty-five basis point hike in December followed by another twenty-five basis point hike in March 2027. If that materializes, deposit beta assumptions embedded in 2027 budget models constructed in October become stale almost immediately.
DataTrek co-founder Nicholas Colas argues that equity market volatility is doing heavy lifting for the Fed and may remove the need for subsequent hikes next year, with futures seeing the market action as reducing the central bank's need to intervene. After the expected December hike, markets forecast the Fed will stay the course through at least the first quarter of 2027, with chances of the next increase not considered likely until April. Overall odds of a more hawkish rate policy have diminished, with odds for no or one hike in 2027 at sixty-eight percent, up from fifty-seven percent a week prior. This creates a genuine fork in bank NIM planning: asset-liability committees must model both a March follow-through and a prolonged pause simultaneously.
---
### Regulatory Radar
The US Basel III Endgame saw its biggest turn in 2026: the original 2023 proposal was effectively scrapped and replaced with something far less aggressive. The 2026 framework introduced the Expanded Risk-Based Approach, removing the requirement for the largest banks to calculate capital under two parallel methodologies simultaneously.
The public comment period closed on June eighteenth, 2026, and no specific effective date has yet been set for the final rule. Status: unchanged from last week. What is new is the article analysis published by Holland and Knight this month in the Journal of Federal Agency Action, which notes the 2026 proposals formally rescind the 2023 framework and notably bring activities such as mortgage origination and servicing back within the agencies' regulatory perimeter.
For Category I and II banks, the Basel III Endgame re-proposal is projected to require banks to hold one point six percent more capital, far less than the 2023 proposal, which would have increased required capital by nine percent for Category I through IV banks.
Also from the November sixth BBVA Research financial regulation weekly: the OCC issued a supervisory framework on bank use of Super Intelligence, and separately, the BCBS is consulting on consequential amendments to the Basel Framework, with a comment deadline of December twenty-first, 2026. Finance transformation leaders should track the December twenty-first BCBS comment deadline, as it may shape the final rule timeline.
---
### AI in Finance
The most consequential development this week is not a vendor announcement -- it is the Capgemini data quantifying the agentic AI value gap. Financial institutions are moving beyond isolated agentic AI experiments to multi-agent AI across core banking and insurance workflows, but the pressure to prove value is intensifying. Roughly half of financial services firms cannot consistently demonstrate a return on their agentic AI initiatives and lack clear frameworks for assessing whether those initiatives deliver sufficient value to justify continued investment. Only five percent of those surveyed have already institutionalized the capabilities required to operate agentic AI at enterprise scale.
The buying signal embedded in this data: firms are converging on a hybrid sourcing model for agentic AI capabilities that balances building capabilities in-house for differentiation, buying packaged agentic solutions to accelerate deployment at scale, and working with partners for ecosystem depth. For finance transformation vendors -- OneStream, Oracle, Workday, BlackLine -- the implication is that packaged agentic capabilities with demonstrable ROI metrics are becoming a purchasing prerequisite, not a differentiator.
A separate PYMNTS Intelligence report adds granularity to where CFOs draw the line on AI autonomy: fifty-two percent of CFOs would use autonomous AI to recommend changes to liquidity or payment timing, but fewer than one in three would allow AI to reallocate budgets. Close to seven percent of enterprise CFOs had deployed agentic AI in finance workflows and five percent were running pilots as of September 2025. Deployment rates remain low; the advice-versus-action distinction is where bank governance frameworks are being drawn.
The macro-AI linkage flagged by Barkin is new terrain: the Richmond Fed president said in prepared remarks on November ninth that the massive wave of AI infrastructure spending is actively adding to near-term inflation by driving robust demand. For bank CFOs building capital expenditure assumptions and long-range plans, this means AI investment is not just a cost-efficiency story but a macro feedback loop they must model explicitly.
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
The rate-path fork described above is the most immediate FP&A demand driver. Banks whose 2027 planning cycles assumed a single December hike and then a prolonged pause must now run a parallel scenario with a March 2027 follow-through. That is not a small revision: it changes deposit cost curves, loan repricing assumptions, funding mix targets, and the efficiency ratio trajectory simultaneously.
The Capgemini ROI finding creates a new buying filter. Finance transformation clients asking about agentic AI investments should now be asked: does the vendor provide a pre-built ROI measurement framework, or are you building governance and measurement from scratch? The five percent who have scaled agentic AI did so with structured frameworks, not exploratory pilots.
KPMG's webcast series from March 2026, "The Agentic Close: From Month-End Sprint to Always-Ready Finance," highlighted how coordinated AI agents can orchestrate an end-to-end financial close process. This is now a live purchasing conversation, not a theoretical one, as banks look to compress close cycles while managing flat-to-declining finance headcount against rising workloads from regulatory reporting demands.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The consensus framing treats today's CPI as a binary December-hike trigger. The more interesting signal is in what happens to market pricing if core comes in at zero point two percent exactly -- consensus -- with no surprise either way. In that scenario, the eighty-four percent December hike odds stay locked in, the market's attention shifts entirely to the March 2027 question, and bank CFOs who front-ran deposit repricing in Q3 on the assumption of a December-then-pause cycle face an uncomfortable realization: they may have locked in funding costs and balance sheet positioning for a tightening cycle that is not finished. The risk is not a hot print; it is a benign print that leaves every planning assumption intact but quietly extends the duration of the problem.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **The March 2027 scenario:** "Your 2027 budget was built assuming December is the last hike. UBS and the Mortgage Bankers Association both see a March follow-through. What does your NIM model look like if deposit costs keep climbing into Q2 2027, and how quickly can your FP&A infrastructure re-run that scenario?"
2. **The agentic AI ROI gap:** "Capgemini just published that half of financial services firms can't demonstrate ROI on agentic AI and only five percent have scaled to enterprise level. Before your next vendor conversation, do you have a measurement framework that would put you in that five percent, or are you in the fifty percent flying blind?"
3. **AI infrastructure as an inflation input:** "Richmond Fed President Barkin is now connecting AI capital spending to near-term inflation pressures. If the Fed is partly hiking because of tech investment demand, your AI transformation budget and your rate environment are no longer independent variables. How are you modeling that in your long-range plan?"
